units.tr: From a letter written on 20 August 1645 by the Author to his brother, who (from London, where he lives) supplied the copy he had of his writing.

units.la: J'Ay escrit ce petit traitté que vous avés (apres plusieurs autres) copié, non à dessein dele rendre public, c'est trop peu de chose; mais en intention de satisfaire au desir de ceux qui avoient voulu s'informer de mon sentiment, touchant un conte d'autant plus digne de donner du soupçon, qu'il s'estoit (sans aucun juste fondement)rendu fort commun. Quantà ce que l'on vous a dit de l'edition d'Anastase, dont on pretend qu'il a esté malignement retranché, voicy ce que j'en ay appris dés l'an 1640. Marc Velser l'undes principaux Magistrats d'Ausbourg, ayant envoyé l'an 1601 aux Jesuites de Mayence, le manuscrit d'Anastase, pour le faire mettre sous la presse; ils prierent Marquard Freher Conseiller de son Altesse Electorale à Heidelberg, de les aider en ce sujet ; sous la promesse qu'ils faisoient de donner au public de bonne foy,ce qui leur seroit communiqué,il leur envoya deux manuscrits d'Anastase, où la vie de la pretendue Papesse se trouvoit. Mais ces Messieurs se contentans de faire tirer deux exemplaires de cette sorte, ils supprimerent dans le reste de l'edition, ce qui leur avoit esté fourni; tellement qu'il n'a point paru, & Monsieur Freher a esté contraint de se plaindre,par une espece de manifeste imprimé,du tour qui luy avoit esté joüé. Je ne pretens pas revoquer rien en doute, de la foy de tout ce recit,partant de personnes qui me sont en telle consideration, que je croirois ne pouvoir (sans me mesconnoistre moy mesme,& blesser l'estime que j'ay tousjours fait de leur tresgrand merite) en venir là. Mais je n'ay jamais veu concevoir que les eloges de Sergius II, Leon IV, & Benoist III, escrits par Anastase, contiennent ce que nous y lifons, & qui est confirmé par tout ce qui nous reste d'auteurs contemporains, & qu'il ait escrit, ou peu escrire, ce que portent les eloges de ce Iean,femelle,que l'on pense avoir occupé le siege Papal entre Leon IV & Benoist III. I'avois donc des lors un tresparticulier regret de ce que personne ne pouvant monstrer ni l'escrit de Monsieur Freher contre les Iesuites, ni les exemplaires qu'ils avoient fait imprimer pour luy, ni en fin ceux qu'il avoit fournis de la Bibliotheque d'Heydelberg, qui sans doute ont esté ensevelis dans les ruines du Palatinat, ou transportés par les Bavarois où il leur a pleu, nous demeurions privés du moyen d'apprendre ce qu'ils pouvoient contenir.
units.tr: I wrote this little treatise, which you have copied (after several others), not intending to make it public, for it is too slight a thing, but to satisfy the wish of those who wanted to learn my opinion on a story all the more likely to arouse suspicion because, without any sound foundation, it has become quite common. As to what you were told about Anastasius's edition, from which it is claimed that the passage was maliciously removed, this is what I have learned since 1640. Marcus Velser, one of the principal magistrates of Augsburg, sent the manuscript of Anastasius to the Jesuits of Mainz in 1601, so that it might be put to press. They asked Marquard Freher, councillor of his Electoral Highness at Heidelberg, to help them in this matter, promising to publish in good faith whatever was communicated to them. He sent them two manuscripts of Anastasius in which the life of the so-called Papess was found. But these gentlemen, content to have only two copies of this kind printed, suppressed in the rest of the edition what had been supplied to them, so that it never appeared, and Monsieur Freher was forced to complain, by a sort of manifesto printed, about the trick that had been played on him. I do not intend to call into doubt the faith of this whole account, given by persons who are held in such esteem by me that I could not (without misjudging myself and damaging the high regard I have always had for their very great merit) come to that. But I have never been able to conceive that the eulogies of Sergius II, Leo IV and Benedict III, written by Anastasius, contain what we read in them, which is confirmed by everything that remains to us from contemporary authors, and that he wrote, or could have written, what the eulogy of this John, the female, supposed to have occupied the papal see between Leo IV and Benedict III, reports. I had therefore from that time a very particular regret that, since no one can show either Monsieur Freher's writing against the Jesuits, or the copies they had printed for him, or finally those he had supplied from the Heidelberg library, which were no doubt buried in the ruins of the Palatinate or carried off by the Bavarians wherever they pleased, we were deprived of the means of learning what they might contain.

units.la: Mais depuis un mois ou environ s'est rencontré icy dans la Bibliotheque du Roy, un manuscrit d'environ deux censans, en beau velin, & en caracteres bien & curieusement peints, qui semble nous devoir donner esclaircissement, touchant le contenu des deux qui avoient esté en la disposition tant de Monsieur Freher,que des Iesuites de Mayence.Car encore que ceux qui l'ont manié les premiers, l'ayent pris pour un Platine, neantmoins c'est en effet un Anastase, à la suite duquel on a adjoufté plusieurs éloges des Papes posterieurs à Nicolas premier ; & qui est en quelques endroits (notamment es vies de Leon IV & Benoist III) plus court que celuy qui a esté imprimé à Mayence, & depuis inseré es editions de Rome, Cologne, & Paris, dans les Tomes des Conciles. Apres cette descouverte,dont tous les esprits curieux ont desiré de satisfaire leur veüe, j'ay tasché (comme les autres) d'en avoir ma part,& ay consideré le tout le plus attentivement qu'il m'a esté possible ; en fin l'ayant leu & releu,j'ay trouvé que l'eloge de la pretendue Papesse est tissu des propres paroles de Martinus Polonus, penitentier d'Innocent IV, & Archevesque de Cosenza, auteur posterieur à Anastase de 400 ans,& de plus fort facile au debit de toutes sortes de fables. Car afin que l'on ne puisse se figurer qu'il ayt transcrit , soit d'Anastase , soit d'aucun autre qui ayt vescu depuis l'an 900,ce qu'il a inseré dans sa Chronique, le discours qui se trouve aujourd'huy mal enchassé dans celuy d'Anastase le justifie, tant par sa conformité avec l'idiome de Martinus Polonus, que par les choses qu'il suppose sans crainte qu'elles fervent à la conviction de l'imposture ; entr'autres que la pretendue Papesse fut dans l'aage de son adolescence menée en habit d'homme à Athenes,où elle profita en diverses sciences; comme si du temps d'Anastase Athenes avoient esté frequentées de Latins , & celebres par l'estude des bonnes lettres ; item qu'elle fit à Rome lecture par trois ans, ou des trois voyes ; (c'est à dire , de la Theologie,du Droit,& de laPhilosophie, qui comprenoit lors la Medicine; à cause de quoy les Medecins sont dans les titres de ce temps là appellés Physiciens;) & eut de grands Maistres pour disciples ; ce qui derechef ne peut convenir au siecle d'Anastase , durant lequel il n'estoit mention,ni d'Universitéz dressées, ni de cours soit en Theologie, soit es arts,soit es autres facultez, ni de terme limité pour chaque cours,ni de qualifier ceux qui enseignoient en quelque sorte que ce fut legentes , ni enfin de passer des Maistres soit en la faculté des arts , soit es autres superieures ; au lieu que tout cela quadre d'autant plus parfaitement au siecle de Martinus Polonus,que nos François ayans conquis Constantinople le Lundy 12 Auril 1204,& l'ayans gardée sous cinq Empereurs des maisons de Flandres & de Courtenay jusques au 25 Juillet Indiction 4, achevant l'an 1261 ; ont possedé en mesme temps le royaume de Thessalonique par des Princes de la maison de Montferrat; la principauté de la Morée, par des Seigneurs des familles de Villehardouin,& de Savoye; & le Duché d'Athenes , par les aisnez de la maison de Brienne,dont le dernier est mort l'an 1347 en Juillet; que ces Princes Latins ont tiré dans leurs Estats quantité de Latins , qui y ont ont porté les mœurs de leur pays , & la forme des estudes : que des le temps de l'Empereur Lothaire mort le 3 Decemb. 1138 , les Universitez avoyent commencé de s'establir tant en France qu'en Italie ; & que des lors les Scolastiques ont eu la vogue , qui ont fait les cours de leurs leçons en trois ans , ont qualifié leurs professeurs Lectores , & Legentes , & ont donné à leurs disciples les degrez de Maistrife , Licence , & Doctorat , mettans en usage des nouvcautez[?] dont jamais les siecles precedents n'avoient ouy parler. Joignez à cela , que dans les eloges de Leon IV & Benoist III , tels que nous les donne le manuscrit de la Bibliotheque Royale enflé du Roman de la Papesse , se trouvent les mesmes termes qu'en l'edition de Mayence: d'où s'ensuit necessairement , que (selon l'intention d'Anastase , violée par la temerite de ceux qui l'ont meslée de leurs songes,) il est absolument impossible,qu'aucun ayt tenu le Papat entre Leon IV & Benoist III. car il dit,qu'apres que le Prelat Leon fut soustrait de cette lumiere, (mox) aušsi tost,tout le Clergé, les notables & le peuple de Rome ont arresté d'elire Benoist: qu'aussi tost (illicò) ils ont efté le trouver, priant dans le titre de S. Callifte, & qu'apres l'avoir assis sur le throne pontifical, & signé le decret de son election,ils l'ont envoyé aux tres-invincibles Augustes Lothaire & Louys: dont le premier (par la confession de tous les Auteurs du temps) est mort le 29 Septembre 8ʒ5, 74 jours apres le Pape Leon. Tout cela non seulement m'empeche de changer d'advis, mais me contraint de plaindre le defavantage de ceux qui (se laissans preoccuper par la hardiesse des imposteurs,qui ont brouille de leurs songes les Auteurs dont ils se sont saisis,) ont de la peine à se desfaire des prejugéz qu'à tresgrand tort ils leur ont fait prendre.
units.tr: But about a month ago, a manuscript of roughly two hundred years' age turned up here in the King's Library, written on fine vellum, with characters beautifully and carefully painted, which seems likely to clear up what the two copies in the hands of Monsieur Freher and of the Jesuits of Mainz contained. For although those who first handled it took it for a Platina, it is in fact an Anastasius, to which several eulogies of popes later than Nicholas I have been appended; in some places (notably in the lives of Leo IV and Benedict III) it is shorter than the one printed at Mainz, and afterwards inserted in the editions of Rome, Cologne and Paris, in the volumes of the Councils. After this discovery, which all curious minds have desired to see for themselves, I tried (like the others) to have my share, and I examined the whole as attentively as I could; in the end, having read and reread it, I found that the eulogy of the so-called Papess is woven from the very words of Martin of Poland, penitentiary of Innocent IV and archbishop of Cosenza, an author four hundred years later than Anastasius, and moreover one who readily dispensed every kind of fable. For lest anyone imagine that he copied what he inserted into his Chronicle either from Anastasius or from any other writer who lived after 900, the passage that now sits awkwardly within Anastasius's text proves it, both by its agreement with the idiom of Martin of Poland and by the things it asserts without fear that they would serve to convict the imposture. Among them: that the so-called Papess, in her adolescence, was taken dressed as a man to Athens, where she profited in various sciences, as if in Anastasius's day Athens had been frequented by Latins and famous for the study of good letters; likewise that she gave lectures in Rome for three years, on the three ways (that is, theology, law and philosophy, which then included medicine, which is why physicians are called physicists in the titles of that time), and had great masters as her pupils; which again cannot suit the age of Anastasius, in which there was no mention of universities established, nor of courses either in theology, the arts or the other faculties, nor of a fixed term for each course, nor of qualifying those who taught as readers in any sense, nor finally of passing from one level to another in the faculty of arts or in the higher faculties. Whereas all this fits perfectly the age of Martin of Poland, since our Franks, having conquered Constantinople on Monday, 12 April 1204, held it under five emperors of the houses of Flanders and Courtenay until 25 July, indiction 4, in the year 1261; at the same time they possessed the kingdom of Thessalonica through princes of the house of Montferrat, the principality of the Morea through lords of the families of Villehardouin and Savoy, and the duchy of Athens through the elder line of the house of Brienne, the last of whom died in July 1347. These Latin princes drew into their states a great number of Latins, who brought there the customs of their country and the form of their studies. From the time of the Emperor Lothair, who died on 3 December 1138, universities had begun to be established both in France and in Italy, and from then on the Schoolmen came into fashion, who arranged their lessons into courses of three years, called their professors "lecturers" and "readers," and gave their pupils the degrees of master, licence and doctorate, bringing into use novelties of which earlier centuries had never heard. Add to this that in the eulogies of Leo IV and Benedict III, as the manuscript of the Royal Library gives them, swollen with the novel of the Papess, the same words are found as in the Mainz edition. From this it necessarily follows that (according to Anastasius's intention, violated by the rashness of those who mixed it with their dreams) it is absolutely impossible that anyone held the papacy between Leo IV and Benedict III. For he says that after the prelate Leo was taken from this light, (mox) immediately the whole clergy, the notables and the people of Rome resolved to elect Benedict; that at once (illicò) they went to find him, praying in the title of St Callixtus, and that after seating him on the papal throne and signing the decree of his election, they sent him to the most invincible Augusti, Lothair and Louis, of whom the first (by the testimony of all the authors of the time) died on 29 September 855, seventy-four days after Pope Leo. All this not only prevents me from changing my opinion, but compels me to pity the disadvantage of those who, preoccupied by the boldness of the impostors who have muddled the authors they laid hands on with their dreams, find it hard to rid themselves of the prejudices which, to their great wrong, they were led to adopt.

units.la: FAMILIER - ESCLAIRCISSEMENT DE LA QUESTION Si une femme a esté assise au Siege Papal de Rome entre Leon IV, & Benoist III.
units.tr: A Familiar Clarification of the Question Whether a Woman Sat on the Papal See of Rome between Leo IV and Benedict III.

units.la: SI (pour avoir subject de le croire) il pouvoit suffire de s'en rapporter à la pluralité des voix de ceux qui ont esté dans cette opinion depuis 550 ans ; la difficulté que l'on en fait aujourd'huy seroit fort facile à resoudre. Car (à prendre du temps que l'on a commencé de parler de la Papesse) nul n'y a formellement contredit, avant Enea Silvio Piccolhomini Evesque de Siene, puis Cardinal du titre de S. Sabine, & en fin Pape Pie II, qui remarquoit le 20 Aoust 1451 à Juan de Carvajal Cardinal de S. Ange, pour conclusion de sa repartie à Nicolas Evesque des Taborites, qu'en l'establissement de cette femme il n'y avoit point eu d'erreur de foy, ny de droit, mais ignorance du fait; qu'aussi l'histoire n'en estoit pas certaine. Environ l'an 1524 & 1556 Iean Thurmaïr d'Avenspergh, appellé ordinairement Aventin, & Michel Buchinger de Colmar, ont suivi la mesme piste, & tiré apres eux la plus grande foule des Docteurs de l'Eglise Romaine.
units.tr: If (to have a ground for believing it) it could be enough to rely on the majority of voices of those who have held this opinion for 550 years, the difficulty people make of it today would be very easy to resolve. For (from the time when people began to speak of the Papess) no one contradicted it formally before Aeneas Silvius Piccolomini, Bishop of Siena, then Cardinal of the title of St Sabina, and finally Pope Pius II. On 20 August 1451, in concluding his reply to Nicholas, Bishop of the Taborites, he remarked to Juan de Carvajal, Cardinal of St Angelo, that in the establishment of this woman there had been no error of faith or of law, but ignorance of the fact; and the history of it was not certain. Around the years 1524 and 1556, Johannes Thurmair of Abensberg, commonly called Aventinus, and Michael Buchinger of Colmar followed the same track, and drew after them the greatest crowd of the teachers of the Roman Church.
