units.la: Or comme ce que la pluspart de ces Messieurs ont precedé Luther, & que tous sont morts dans la communion de Rome, prouve demonstrativement que mal à propos & ridiculement on cherche l'origine de la supposition entre les Protestans,qui n'ont jamais fait estat que d'acquiescer sans examen,à ce que tant d'hommes doctes & partisans des Papes avoient asseuré à l'enuy , ne pouvant presumer que le certificat constant d'un si grand nombre de gens bien sensez deust estre revoqué en doute, ni qu'il leur fust arrivé de se mesprendre à leur propre prejudice, & combattre(sans y penser)la verité,en confessant , à fausses enseignes, des choses qui leur tournoient à honte. Ce qu'ils se sont accordez à placer leur Papesse entre Leon IV & Benoist III, demonstre insurmontablement que leur intention uniforme a esté de luy donner quartier entre l'an 852 & 858 de nostre Seigneur ; & que ceux qui entreprendroient aujourd'huy de franchir ces termes, auroient, (comme auteurs d'opinions singulieres, & seuls de leur parti) à passer pour extravagans.
units.tr: Now, since most of these gentlemen wrote before Luther, and all died in the communion of Rome, it demonstrates that it is wrong and absurd to look for the origin of the fabrication among the Protestants. They never made it their practice to acquiesce without examination in what so many learned men and partisans of the Popes had eagerly assured one another. Nor could they presume that the constant testimony of so great a number of sensible people should be called in doubt, or that they could have been mistaken to their own prejudice, and, without thinking, combated the truth by confessing, under false colours, things that turned to their shame. That they all agreed in placing their Papess between Leo IV and Benedict III demonstrates insurmountably that their uniform intention was to give her a place between the years 852 and 858 of our Lord. And those who would undertake today to step beyond these limits would have to be considered extravagant, as authors of singular opinions and alone in their party.

units.la: En effet je ne voy que la seule histoire d'Erford, qui parlant de Iean VIII I I[?] successeur d'Adrian I I, & predecesseur de Marin I, entre le 1 Novemb. 872, & le 14 Decembre 882, use de ces paroles: Notez que ce Pape a esté femme, & seroit le huitieme du nom de Iean, s'il estoit compté entre les autres. Mais en cela elle s'est eloignée du sentiment de Marianus Scotus, & de tous les autres qui l'ont suivi. Et ne faut pas penser que ceux qui ont appellé le predecesseur de la pretendue Papesse Leon cinquieme, & elle mesme Iean septieme, ayent eu une autre visée que le commun. Car Martinus Polonus, Conradus Halberstadiensis, Hermannus Cygneus, Suffridus Petri, Compilatio Chronologica, & autres, appellent Leon cinquieme celuy qui n'estoit que quatrieme, ou pource qu'ils ont estimé que Gregoire IV portoit aussi le nom de Leon, ou pource qu'à l'imitation de Sigebert, Vincent de Beauvais & Albert Abbé de Staden, ils s'estoient imaginé, qu'un certain Leon qui ne fut jamais, avoit succedé à Felix second, Antipape de Liberius environ l'an 357, & que le mesme avoit persecuté nostre grand S. Hilaire: & Iacques Philippe Forest de Bergame, Raphael de Volterra, Sabellicus, & autres ont donné à leur Papesse le nom de Jean septiéme; pource qu'ils n'ont point fait de distinction entre Jean sixiéme & Jean septiéme; qui ont tenu le Papat l'un apres l'autre immediatement; le premier depuis le Dimanche 30 Octob. de l'an 701, jusques au 7 Janvier de l'an 705; & le second depuis le Dimanche 1 May de l'an 705, jusques au 16 Oct. de l'an 707. D'où resulte necessairement, que ces deux bandes d'Auteurs qui semblent se tirer à quartier, & contredire à l'opinion commune, concernant le temps de la pretendue Papesse, l'establissent au fonds, & difent la mesme chose que les autres, quoy que d'une differente maniere; pource qu'outre le prejugé commun qui les avoit preoccupez, ils avoient leurs beveuës particulieres, aufquelles les autres escrivains n'avoient point donné de lieu. Et pourtant ils se determinent tous egalement, & sans dissentiment, donnant à leur Jeanne, Leon pour predecesseur, & Benoist pour successeur, & se reduisant au temps qui a coulé entre l'an 852 & l'an 858.
units.tr: Indeed, I see only the history of Erfurt, which, speaking of John VIII, successor of Adrian II and predecessor of Marinus I, between 1 November 872 and 14 December 882, uses these words: Note that this Pope was a woman, and would be the eighth of the name of John, if she were counted among the others. But in this it departs from the opinion of Marianus Scotus and of all the others who followed him. Nor should one think that those who called the predecessor of the so-called Papess Leo V, and she herself John VII, had any other aim than the common one. For Martinus Polonus, Conradus Halberstadiensis, Hermannus Cygneus, Suffridus Petri, Compilatio Chronologica, and others call Leo V him who was only the fourth, either because they thought Gregory IV also bore the name Leo, or because, imitating Sigebert, Vincent of Beauvais and Albert, Abbot of Stade, they imagined that a certain Leo, who never existed, had succeeded Felix II, antipope to Liberius, around the year 357, and had persecuted our great St Hilary. And Jacopo Filippo Foresti of Bergamo, Raffaele of Volterra, Sabellicus and others gave their Papess the name John VII, because they made no distinction between John VI and John VII, who held the papacy one immediately after the other: the first from Sunday 30 October 701 until 7 January 705, and the second from Sunday 1 May 705 until 16 October 707. From this it necessarily follows that these two bands of authors, who seem to shelter themselves and contradict the common opinion concerning the time of the so-called Papess, in substance establish it and say the same thing as the others, although in a different way. For, besides the common prejudice that had preoccupied them, they had their own particular errors, to which the other writers had given no occasion. And therefore they all determine equally, and without dissent, giving to their Joan Leo as predecessor and Benedict as successor, and confining themselves to the time that ran between the year 852 and the year 858.

units.la: Cela presuppose, quatre choses sont à remarquer, pour mener asseurement les esprits à la connoissance exacte de la verité. La premiere, que le conte de la Papesse a esté conceu fort tard; car (par la confession de tous) Benoist III que l'on pretend avoir pris sa place a tenu le Siege avant l'an 858; & Marianus Scotus (le premier de tous ceux qui ont jamais parlé d'elle) {1} est nay (selon la remarque de Florent de Worcester) l'an 1028, & il nous atteste de foy mesme qu'il fit sa profession à Cologne le Jeudy 1 Aoust 1056, fut sacré Prestre à Wirtsbourg, le Samedy 13 Mars 1058; renfermé à Fulde le 14 May suivant, qui estoit le Vendredy d'apres l'Ascension; & renclos pour la seconde fois à Mayence, le Vendredy 3 Auril 1069. Joint que Dodechin son continuateur, asseure qu'il a esté inhumé à S. Martin de Mayence l'an 1086, qui estoit le 230 apres l'establissement solennel de Benoist troisiesme, arrivé (comme il sera demonstré cy apres) le Dimanche 29 Septembre l'an 855.
units.tr: That presupposes four things to be noted, if minds are to be led securely to exact knowledge of the truth. The first is that the story of the Papess was conceived very late. For (by everyone's admission) Benedict III, whom they claim took her place, held the See before the year 858. Marianus Scotus, the first of all who ever spoke of her, {1} was born (according to the remark of Florence of Worcester) in the year 1028. He himself attests that he made his profession at Cologne on Thursday 1 August 1056, was ordained priest at Würzburg on Saturday 13 March 1058, was shut up at Fulda on 14 May following, which was the Friday after the Ascension, and was enclosed a second time at Mainz on Friday 3 April 1069. Moreover, Dodechin, his continuator, asserts that he was buried at St Martin's in Mainz in the year 1086, which was the 230th year after the solemn enthronement of Benedict III, which took place (as will be demonstrated below) on Sunday 29 September 855.

units.la: La seconde, que ce mesme conte a esté tout composé de pieces de rapport, & enrichi avec le temps. Car voicy ce que Marianus avoit escrit sur l'an 855, de nostre Seigneur, qui estoit le 13 de l'Empereur Lothaire: Le Pape Leon meurt le 1 d'Aoust. A cettuy cy a succedé Jeanne femme, durant deux ans, cinq mois, quatre jours. Mais Martinus Polonus decedé environ l'an 1270, c'est à dire, 184 ans apres la mort de Marianus, & 425 apres l'inthronization de Benoist III; s'est advisé de dire que la Ieanne de Marianus s'appelloit l'Anglois, qu'elle estoit de la nation de Mayence, qu'ayant esté engrossée, elle accoucha en pleine procession, entre S. Clement & le Colisée, & qu'en detestation de son crime, la procession (prenant un destour) a cessé de passer par cette rüe là. Thierry de Niem qui a escrit immediatement devant le Concile de Constance, assemblé premierement le Vendredy 16 Decemb. 1413 (environ 328 ans apres la mort de Marianus, & 559 apres l'inthronization de Benoist,)adjoufte du sien qu'une statue a esté erigée en memoire de cet accident. Guillaume Breuin qui a escrit {1} des VII principales Eglises de Rome, & Baptiste Platine qui est mort l'an 1481,395 ans apres la mort de Marianus, & 626 apres l'elevement de Benoist III (pour enfler la dose) ont mis en avant la selle persée, sur laquelle (à leur dire[?]) le Pape doit estre assis pour estre manié[?]. Et plus de cent ans apres, d'autres ont trouvé à propos de contribuer du leur, asseurant que la pretendue Ieanne estoit Magicienne, qu'elle a couronné l'Empereur Louys second &c. tellement qu'à peine 460 ans ont peu suffire pour donner l'entiere forme à cet ours, dont le pauvre Marianus s'estoit (je ne sçay comment) deschargé. D'où en ont tant appris ceux qui estoient venus les derniers ? & comment leur est il arrivé de rendre leur pretendue histoire plus complete ; sinon en puisant', chacun à discretion, de ses propres imaginations ?
units.tr: The second is that this same tale was entirely made up of borrowed pieces and enriched over time. For this is what Marianus wrote under the year 855 of our Lord, which was the 13th year of the Emperor Lothar: Pope Leo dies on 1 August. To him succeeded Joan, a woman, for two years, five months, four days. But Martin of Poland, who died around the year 1270, that is, 184 years after the death of Marianus and 425 after the enthronement of Benedict III, took it into his head to say that Marianus's Joan was called the Englishwoman, that she was of the nation of Mainz, that having been made pregnant she gave birth in the middle of a procession between St Clement's and the Colosseum, and that, in detestation of her crime, the procession (taking a detour) has ceased to pass along that street. Thierry de Niem, who wrote immediately before the Council of Constance, first assembled on Friday 16 December 1413 (about 328 years after the death of Marianus and 559 after the enthronement of Benedict), adds on his own account that a statue was erected in memory of this incident. William Breuin, who wrote {1} on the seven principal churches of Rome, and Platina, who died in 1481, 395 years after the death of Marianus and 626 after the elevation of Benedict III, (to swell the dose) put forward the perforated chair, on which (so they say[?]) the Pope must sit to be examined[?]. And more than a hundred years later, others thought fit to contribute their own, asserting that the so-called Joan was a sorceress, and that she crowned the Emperor Louis II, &c. So that scarcely 460 years have sufficed to give final shape to this bear, of which poor Marianus had (I know not how) rid himself. From where did those who came last learn so much? And how did it come about that they made their so-called history more complete, except by drawing, each at his own pleasure, on his own imaginations?

units.la: La troisiéme remarque doit estre,qu'entre l'an 855 auquel Benoist a esté elevé au Papat, l'an 1056 auquel Marianus Scotus a esté reçeu profez à Cologne , & l'an 1414 auquel le Concile de Constance a esté sus pieds , plusieurs personnages demarque ont laissé des monumens qui infirment tout ce que Marianus, & ceux qui l'ont suivi, ont advancé touchant le Pontificat de la pretendue Jeanne. Par exemple Loup Abbé de S. Joffe sur la mer, & de Bethlehem , ou de Ferrieres prés Montargis , qui s'est trouvé au Concile assemblé le 26 d'Auril 853 à Soissons. Le Concile assemblé à Sablonieres pres de Toul l'an 859. Le Pape Nicolas I qui a tenu le Siege apres Benoist III pretendu successeur de Jeanne. Hincmar promeu à l'Archevesché de Rheïms l'an 845 en Auril , sacré le Dimanche 17 May suivant , & decedé le 21 Decembre 882. Ado qui a succedé en l'Archevesché de Vienne à Agilmar decedé le 6 Juillet 859,a foufcrit au Concile assemblé à Toufy prés de Toul le 21 Octobre 860; & est decedé environ l'an 872; veu que Otram son successeur a signé les decrets du Concile assemblé l'an 876 en Fevrier dans le Palais de Pontyon pres Vitry. Anastafe Abbé & Bibliothecaire de l'Eglife Romaine qui a dedié la version de la vie de S. Jean l'Aumosnier Patriarche d'Alexandrie, au Pape Nicolas I; celle du Concile assemblé l'an 869 dans Constantinople contre Photius, au Pape Adrian II; & celle du 2 Concile de Nicée au Pape Jean VIII; & qui a esté envoyé en Ambassade à Constantinople par l'Empereur Louys l'an 869 avec le Comte Suppon, les Annales de S. Bertin finissans à l'an 882. Guillaume le Bibliothecaire qui a escrit la vie du Pape Adrian II. Luitprand premierement Diacre de Pavie, & puis Evefque de Cremone, qui a exercé la charge d'Ambassadeur à Constantinople l'an 946 pour Berenger Roy d'Italie II du nom, & l'an 968 pour l'Empereur Otton le grand. Flodoard Curé de Cormicy & Chanoine de Rheims qui est decedé le 28 Mars 966. Herman furnommé Contractus de la famille desComtes deVeringhen, moine de l'Abbaye de Richenaw pres Constance, qui est decedé l'an 1054. Hugues Abbé de Fleuri ou S.Benoist sur Loire, qui est necessairement decedé avant l'an 1059, veu que Rainier son successeur assista avec Isembard Evesque d'Orleans au sacre du Roy Philippe I couronné à Rheims le 27 May jour de Pentecoste audit an. Florent de Worcester qui a vescu environ l'an 1118.Honoré prestre & scholastique d'Austun, qui est mort environ l'an 1130. Nicolaus Maniacutius qui a esté contemporain.Conrad deLicthenaw[?]Abbé d'Vrsperg decedé environ l'an 1229. Albert Abbé de Staden qui a fleuri environ l'an 1240. Vincent de Beauvais decedé l'an 1256. Guillaume de Nangis decedé environ l'an 1302.Matthieu de Westmonstier decedé environ l'an 1370.
units.tr: The third remark must be that between the year 855, in which Benedict was raised to the Papacy, the year 1056, in which Marianus Scotus was received as a professed monk at Cologne, and the year 1414, in which the Council of Constance was dissolved, several notable men left monuments which refute all that Marianus, and those who followed him, have advanced concerning the Pontificate of the so-called Joan. For example: Lupus, Abbot of St Josse-sur-Mer and of Bethlehem, or of Ferrières near Montargis, who was present at the council assembled on 26 April 853 at Soissons; the council assembled at Savonnières near Toul in the year 859; Pope Nicholas I, who held the See after Benedict III, the supposed successor of Joan; Hincmar, promoted to the Archbishopric of Reims in April 845, consecrated on Sunday 17 May following, and who died on 21 December 882; Adon, who succeeded Agilmar as Archbishop of Vienne, Agilmar having died on 6 July 859, who subscribed to the council assembled at Tousey near Toul on 21 October 860, and who died around the year 872, since Otram, his successor, signed the decrees of the council assembled in February 876 in the palace of Ponthion near Vitry; Anastasius, Abbot and Librarian of the Roman Church, who dedicated his version of the life of St John the Almsgiver, Patriarch of Alexandria, to Pope Nicholas I; his version of the council assembled in Constantinople in 869 against Photius, to Pope Hadrian II; and his version of the Second Council of Nicaea to Pope John VIII; and who was sent on embassy to Constantinople by the Emperor Louis in 869 with Count Suppo; and the Annals of St Bertin, which end at the year 882; William the Librarian, who wrote the life of Pope Hadrian II; Liutprand, first a deacon of Pavia and then Bishop of Cremona, who held the office of ambassador at Constantinople in 946 for Berengar II, King of Italy, and in 968 for the Emperor Otto the Great; Flodoard, parish priest of Cormicy and canon of Reims, who died on 28 March 966; Herman, surnamed Contractus, of the family of the Counts of Veringen, a monk of the Abbey of Reichenau near Constance, who died in the year 1054; Hugh, Abbot of Fleury, or of St Benedict-on-Loire, who necessarily died before the year 1059, since Rainier, his successor, assisted with Isembard, Bishop of Orléans, at the consecration of King Philip I, crowned at Reims on 27 May, the Feast of Pentecost, that year; Florence of Worcester, who lived around the year 1118; Honorius, priest and scholastic of Autun, who died around the year 1130; Nicolaus Maniacutius, who was a contemporary; Conrad de Lichtenau[?], Abbot of Ursberg, who died around the year 1229; Albert, Abbot of Stade, who flourished around the year 1240; Vincent of Beauvais, who died in 1256; William of Nangis, who died around the year 1302; Matthew of Westminster, who died around the year 1370.

units.la: Et entre les Grecs Photius elevé au Patriarchat de Constantinople en la place d'Iguace le 22 Decembre 860, & decedé l'an 886.Stylianus Archevesque de Neocesarée sur l'Euphrate, qui a assisté au Concile assemblé l'an 869 contre Photius, & escrit au Pape Estienne V l'an 886.Metrophanes Evesque de Smyrne qui s'est trouvé au Concile assemblé dans Constantinople l'an 869. L'Autheur du livret publié à Constantinople l'an 891 contre la memoire de Photius, & inseré à la fin des actes du Concile assemblé pour le deposseder l'an 869. Outre 4 divers Manuscripts des Grecs disputans contre les Latins touchant la procession du S. Esprit. Seroit-il bien possible, que ces auteurs, plusieurs desquels (comme les Grecs) estoient picquez contre Rome; & d'autres qui ont remarqué quantité de particularitez qui luy estoient peu honorables, non contens d'avoir ou ignoré, ou dissimulé, ou mesmes oublié la plus honteuse de toutes ses disgraces, si jamais elle estoit arrivée, se fussent accordez à fournir (chacun de son costé) des argumens pour en combattre la creance?
units.tr: And among the Greeks: Photius, raised to the Patriarchate of Constantinople in place of Ignatius on 22 December 860, who died in 886; Stylianus, Archbishop of Neocaesarea on the Euphrates, who attended the council assembled in 869 against Photius, and who wrote to Pope Stephen V in 886; Metrophanes, Bishop of Smyrna, who was present at the council assembled in Constantinople in 869; the author of the little book published at Constantinople in 891 against the memory of Photius, inserted at the end of the acts of the council assembled to depose him in 869; besides four different manuscripts of the Greeks disputing with the Latins concerning the procession of the Holy Spirit. Could it really be possible that these authors, many of whom (like the Greeks) were embittered against Rome, and others who noted a great number of particulars that were not very honourable to it, not content to have either ignored, or dissembled, or even forgotten the most shameful of all its disgraces, if it had ever occurred, would all have agreed to supply (each from his own side) arguments to combat belief in it?

units.la: Pour 4 r'addresse, faut prendre garde que Marianus(la phantasie ou l'incurie duquel a esté la premiere matrice où la Papesse a pris sa forme) convient avec ceux qui l'impugnent, de certaines hypotheses confessées par tous, & de la presuppossition desquelles resulte de toute necessité la conviction de son erreur. Par exemple que Leon IV a esté promeu apres Sergius II au Papat l'an 847: qu'il a tenu le Siege 8 ans: & que l'Empereur Lothaire a quitté l'empire pour se charger du froc monastique dans l'Abbaye de Prom prés de Treves, & y est mort le Samedy 28, ou le Dimanche 29 Septembre 855. Voila pourquoy (les ayant fermement establies comme des principes communs & indifputables, par le rapport des suffrages que les plus proches du temps ont laissez à la bonne foy de la posterité) il sera aisé de prouver irrefragablement la succession immediate de Benoist III, apres Leon IV: & en suite, confondre (par l'evidence d'une verité claire comme le Midy) les beveües de Marianus, source unique & primitive de tous ceux qui ont interposé la pretendue Jeanne.
units.tr: For my fourth point, one must be careful that Marianus, whose fancy or carelessness was the first matrix in which the Papess took her form, agrees with those who oppose him on certain hypotheses that all confess, and from whose presupposition the refutation of his error follows of necessity. For example: that Leo IV was promoted to the Papacy after Sergius II in 847; that he held the see for 8 years; and that the Emperor Lothair resigned the empire to take the monastic habit in the abbey of Prüm near Trier, and died there on Saturday 28 or Sunday 29 September 855. That is why, having firmly established these as common and indisputable principles, on the testimony of the witnesses nearest to the time who have left them to the good faith of posterity, it will be easy to prove irrefutably the immediate succession of Benedict III after Leo IV, and then to confound, by the evidence of a truth as clear as noon, the blunders of Marianus, the sole and original source of all who have inserted the supposed Joan.

units.la: Leon IV a esté eleu le propre jour du decez de Sergius I I son predecesseur, voire devant qu'il fust enterré: & de cet evenement arrivé le {1}Mardy 19 Auril, la remarque est expresse en Anastase le Bibliothecaire, auteur contemporain suivi par Luitprand, Bernard Guido Evesque de Lodeve, & la grande Chronique Belgique. Mesme l'on ne peut l'assigner à une autre année qu'à la 847 de nostre Seigneur, de laquelle Marianus & Sigebert convient, pource qu'Anastase parlant du tremblement de terre que Rome ressentit au commencement du Pontificat de Leon, observe qu'elle en receut des atteintes durant l'indiction 10, qui acheva au premier de Septemb. 847: & que le mesme auteur avecHonoré d'Auftun, Matthieu de Weftmonftier,& le Fafciculus temporum, borne le pontificat de Leon dans l'espace de 8 ans, 3 mois, & 5 jours, qui se trouve precisement entre le Mardy 12 Auril 847, & le Mercredy 17 Iuillet 855, jour auquel le Martyrologe Romain,& Anastase, & Luitprand,& Albert Abbé de Staden assignent son trespas. La grande Chronique Belgique apres Bernard Guidon luy donne 8 ans, 3 mois, & 6 jours; en quoy elle s'abuse d'autant plus certainement, qu'elle & le Fasciculus datent sa mort du Mardy 16 Iuillet, & par ce moyen sont tous deux obligez à rabbattre 2 jours des 6 dont ils luy avoyent fait largesse. Luitprand avec Albert de Staden compte 8 ans, 6 mois, & 3 jours, confondant par mesgarde le nombre des mois avec celuy des jours; & faisant(sans y penser) vivre Leon jusques dans le 3 mois de Benoist son successeur, bien loin au delà du 17 Iuillet, auquel l'un & l'autre tient qu'il est mort. Estant impossible que celuy qui a commencé de tenir le siege au 12 Auril, s'il là (comme ils supposent) occupé 8 ans, 6 mois, & trois jours, soit decedé en Juillet , d'où commencoit le 4 mois de sa neufvieme année ; & l'evidence de la raison requerant de toute necessité , qu'en ce cas il ait vescu jusques au Mercredy 15 d'Octobre, 17 jours apres l'inthronization de Benoist qui luy a succedé. Godefroy de Viterbe qui se contente de luy accorder precisement 5 mois outre les 8 ans , est battu par le mesme inconvenient, à scavoir qu'il luy fait terminer son Pontificat dans celuy de Benoist, le Ieudy 12 Septemb. & non le 17 Juillet ; comme le Martyrologe, & les plus anciens requierent.
units.tr: Leo was elected on the very day of the death of Sergius II, his predecessor, indeed before he was buried; and of this event, which occurred on Tuesday {1}19 April, the remark is explicit in Anastasius the Librarian, a contemporary author followed by Luitprand, Bernard Guido bishop of Lodève, and the Great Belgian Chronicle. Moreover, it can be assigned to no other year than 847 of our Lord, on which Marianus and Sigebert agree, because Anastasius, speaking of the earthquake that Rome felt at the beginning of Leo's pontificate, notes that it was felt during the indiction 10, which ended on 1 September 847. The same author, together with Honoré d'Autun, Matthew of Westminster, and the Fasciculus temporum, limits Leo's pontificate to 8 years, 3 months, and 5 days, which falls precisely between Tuesday 12 April 847 and Wednesday 17 July 855, the day on which the Roman Martyrology, Anastasius, Luitprand, and Albert abbot of Stade give his death. The Great Belgian Chronicle, after Bernard Guidon, gives him 8 years, 3 months, and 6 days; in this it errs all the more certainly, since it and the Fasciculus date his death to Tuesday 16 July, and so both are obliged to deduct 2 of the 6 days they had granted him. Luitprand with Albert of Stade counts 8 years, 6 months, and three days, carelessly confusing the number of months with that of days, and making Leo (without realising it) live into the third month of his successor Benedict, well beyond 17 July, on which both agree that he died. For it is impossible that one who began to hold the see on 12 April, if he had occupied it (as they suppose) for 8 years, 6 months, and three days, should have died in July, when the fourth month of his ninth year began; and the evidence of reason requires of necessity that in that case he lived until Wednesday 15 October, 17 days after the enthronement of Benedict, who succeeded him. Godfrey of Viterbo, who is content to grant him precisely 5 months beyond the 8 years, is struck by the same difficulty, namely that he makes Leo's pontificate end within that of Benedict, on Thursday 12 September and not 17 July, as the Martyrology and the oldest authorities require.

units.la: La Compilation Chronologique, se mesurant à la mesme aulne que Godefroy, tombe en une mesprise encore plus insupportable : car elle prend le commencement de Leon , en l'an 844, auquel Sergius son predecefseur vint au Papat ; & par ce moyen s'engage à le faire mourir l'an 852 , à la fin de sa cinquiéme année , & à laisser apres luy un interregne de 4 ans & plus , jusques à Benoist qu'elle eleve sur le siege l'an 856, c'est à dire un an plus tard qu'il ne faut.
units.tr: The Chronological Compilation, measuring by the same yardstick as Godfrey, falls into a mistake even more intolerable: for it takes the beginning of Leo's pontificate to be in 844, the year in which his predecessor Sergius came to the Papacy. By this means it is committed to making him die in 852, at the end of his fifth year, and to leaving an interregnum of four years and more after him, until Benedict, whom it raises to the see in 856, that is a year later than it should be.

units.la: Le Comte Herman attribue à Leon neuf ans , trois mois , & fix jours , pource qu'il rapporte son election à l'an 846 , passé par Sergius son predecesseur de trois mois & 12 jours ;& date {1}encore plus abfurdement sa mort de l'an 856, sans considerer qu'à ce compte il auroit outrepassé 10 ans, & qu'il se trouveroit luy mesme contraint de luy adjouster une année supernumeraire, & le mener jusques dans la seconde de Benoist. Or si cet auteur (autrement digne de loüange) s'est en ce chef fort oublié ; l'Abbé d'Vrsberg (qui a aussi de son costé bien merité de l'histoire) s'est monstré le plus desraisonnable de tous ; entant qu'il date de l'an 857, la mort de Leon IV,faisant hardiment passer son pontificat par delà les dix années, au prejudice de Benoist III, qu'il a reduit à une seule, contre l'advis unanime de tous les autres, qui luy en accordent deux & demie. Et comme j'ay fait rapport de la diversité de leurs advis, pour rendre palpable (à ceux qui les voudroient prendre pour guides) l'egarement de leur raison : ayant à me recueillir, je conclus que cette diversité (quelque jugement que l'on en puisse faire) sert à la convictión de la supposition de Marianus. Veu qu'il demeure constant, que Leon,qui a pris la place de Sergius II l'an 847, & non l'an 853 (comme pretend Florent de Worcester, qui commence son Pontificat de la mesme année en laquelle Marianus a estimé qu'il avoit fini) Leon di-je est d'autant plus necessairement mort l'an 855, qu'il a passé la 8 année de quelques mois, & que ceux qui le font entrer plus avant dans la neufviéme, ou le poufsent jusques à la dixiéme ; combattent par cela mesme plus fortement l'intrusion que l'on a pensé faire d'une je ne sçay quelle Papesse dans son siege apres sa mort ; & roignent[?] partie (plus ou moins grande) du temps que ceux qui l'ont produite luy assignent, pour la durée de son pretendu pontificat.
units.tr: Count Herman attributes to Leo nine years, three months, and six days, because he dates his election to 846, reckoning Sergius his predecessor's reign at three months and 12 days; and he dates Leo's death even more absurdly to 856, without considering that on this reckoning Leo would have exceeded 10 years, and that he himself would be forced to add a supernumerary year and carry Leo on into the second year of Benedict. Now if this author, otherwise worthy of praise, forgot himself so badly on this point, the Abbot of Ursberg, who has also deserved well of history, has shown himself the most unreasonable of all: he dates Leo IV's death to 857, boldly stretching Leo's pontificate beyond the ten years, to the prejudice of Benedict III, whom he reduces to a single year, against the unanimous opinion of all the others, who grant him two and a half. And since I have reported the diversity of their opinions, in order to make plain (to those who would take them for guides) the aberration of their reasoning, I conclude that this diversity, whatever judgement one may make of it, serves to convict Marianus's supposition. For it remains certain that Leo, who took the place of Sergius II in 847 and not in 853 (as Florence of Worcester claims, who begins his pontificate in the same year in which Marianus thought it ended), Leo, I say, is all the more necessarily dead in 855, since he passed the eighth year by some months; and those who carry him further into the ninth, or push him as far as the tenth, by that very fact argue more strongly against the intrusion which was supposed to have been made of some Papess into his see after his death; and they gnaw away at a part (more or less great) of the time which those who produced her assign to her supposed pontificate.

units.la: Quant à la resignation de l'empire faite par Lothaire , & sa mort advenue peu apres, il appert par son Epitaphe escrit de la main de Rabanus Archevesque de Mayence, decedé le 4 Fevrier 856; & par Ado Archevesque de Vienne qui luy a survescu d'environ 16 ans ; & par les Annales de Fulde terminées à l'an 900 ; & par Regino qui coupe son histoire à l'an 906 , & a tenu l'Abbaye de Prom, ou Lothaire a esté reclus & inhumé ; & par l'edition faite en 1618 de la Chronique du Comte Herman, decedé l'an 1054 ; & par Lambert de Schaffnabourg, qui a cessé d'escrire l'an 1068 ; & par Marianus , Sigebert , Godefroy de Viterbe , Vincent de Beauvais , Guillaume de Nangis , la Chronique Australe, Palmerius, Blondus, Aventin, Egnatius, Mutius, le continuateur de Beda ; bref presque par tous, que ce Prince est decedé la nuit d'entre le Samedi 28, & le Dimanche 29 Septembre 855 : & la remarque d'un tel evenement, & l'admirable accord de ceux qui en conviennent, doivent estre d'autant plus considerez, qu'ils battent en ruine le songe de Marianus, voire mettent Marianus aux prises avec soy mesme, comme nous ferons voir cy apres.
units.tr: As for the resignation of the empire made by Lothar, and his death which came soon after, it appears from his epitaph, written by the hand of Rabanus, Archbishop of Mainz, who died on 4 February 856; from Ado, Archbishop of Vienne, who outlived him by about sixteen years; from the Annals of Fulda, ended at the year 900; from Regino, who breaks off his history at the year 906 and held the Abbey of Prüm, where Lothar was shut up and buried; from the edition of the Chronicle of Count Herman made in 1618, who died in 1054; from Lambert of Schaffnaburg, who ceased writing in 1068; and from Marianus, Sigebert, Godfrey of Viterbo, Vincent of Beauvais, William of Nangis, the Chronica Australis, Palmerius, Blondus, Aventinus, Egnatius, Mutius, and the continuator of Bede; in short, from nearly all of them, that this prince died in the night between Saturday 28 and Sunday 29 September 855. The notice of such an event, and the remarkable agreement of those who concur on it, deserve all the more consideration because they overthrow the dream of Marianus, and indeed set Marianus at odds with himself, as we shall show below.

units.la: L'ordre veut maintenant que nous recherchions si Leon IV, estant decedé le 17 Iuillet 855, Benoist III luy a succedé immediatement, ou non. La grande Chronique Belgique (à l'imitation de Bernard Guido) asseure que apres la mort de Leon (qu'elle rapporte au 16 Iuillet un jour plustoft qu'il ne faut) le siege a vacqué six jours : & cela nous meneroit au Dimanche 21 Iuillet ; auquel il y auroit beaucoup plus d'apparence de remettre l'election de Benoist, que non pas au 24 suivant, choisi (sans aucune raison qui nous paroisse) par Ciacconus, qui n'a pas pris garde qu'il escheoit au Mercredy, jour peu convenable à la practique ancienne touchant les elections & ordinations : & que les paroles d'Anastase le Bibliothecaire., descrivant celle de Benoist , semblent y repugner , ces mots {1} aussi tost apres , ne se pouvans commodement entendre,au bout de la huittaine;comme il pretend , & encore moins au bout de la quinzaine , comme {2} le Cardinal Bellarmin & d'autres apres luy se sont imaginez, je ne sçay sur quel fondement.
units.tr: Order now requires us to inquire whether Leo IV, having died on 17 July 855, was immediately succeeded by Benedict III or not. The great Belgian Chronicle (in imitation of Bernard Guido) assures us that after Leo's death (which it places on 16 July, a day earlier than it should be) the see was vacant for six days; and that would bring us to Sunday 21 July, on which day there would be much more likelihood of placing the election of Benedict than on the following 24th, a date chosen by Ciacconius without any reason that seems to us, and who did not notice that it fell on a Wednesday, a day little suited to the ancient practice regarding elections and ordinations. Moreover, the words of Anastasius the Librarian, describing Benedict's election, seem to contradict this: the words {1} soon afterwards cannot conveniently be understood as at the end of a week, as Ciacconius claims, and still less as at the end of a fortnight, as {2} Cardinal Bellarmine and others after him have imagined, I know not on what foundation.

units.la: Albert Abbé de Staden prend autrement ses mesures ; & neantmoins nous conduit certainement au but , disant {3} qu'apres la mort de Leon le Papat cessa deux mois , & douze jours ; qui se trouvent precisement entre le Mercredy 17 Iuillet 855,auquel Leon expira, & le Dimanche 29 Septemb. suivant , auquel Benoist fut solemnellement installé. Anastase , Luitprand , Honoré d'Austun , Godefroy de Viterbe , Albert de Staden , Matthieu de Westmonstier, & le Fasciculus , nous conduisent encore à la verité , mais par un chemin different , entant qu'ils determinent la durée du Pontificat de Benoist III , à deux ans , six mois , & dix jours , que nous avons precisement entre le Dimanche 29 Septembre 855 , jour de l'inthronization dudit Benoist , & le Vendredy huictiéme Auril 858 jour de son decez. Et de ce conte perfonne ne se trouve fort eloigné que l'Abbé. d'Ursperg, qui ne coupe le filé de la vie de Leon qu'à l'an 857, dans les bornes duquel il renferme entierement le Papat de Benoist III, luy retranchant plus de sa juste moitié. Car le Comte Herman (quoy qu'ille commence à l'an 856, & le finisse à l'an 857, & par consequent l'estende à moins de deux ans entiers)ne laisse pas de le borner à deux ans, six mois, neuf jours ; un jour de moins que les autres ; & Marianus qui prend l'origine de sa Prelature de l'an 857, luy accorde deux ans, six mois & six jours; retranchant 4 des 10 qui luy sont deus legitimement. Tout de mesme que Florent de Worcester, qui avoit mal commencé le compte des années de Leon IV à l'an 853, (celuy-là mesme auquel Marianus pretend qu'il est mort) revient à soymesme en comptant l'establissement de Benoist III dans l'an 855, & à cet égard tombe d'accord avec les autres.
units.tr: Albert, Abbot of Stade, takes his measure differently, and yet certainly leads us to the mark, saying {3} that after Leo's death the papacy ceased for two months and twelve days; which fall precisely between Wednesday 17 July 855, on which Leo expired, and Sunday 29 September following, on which Benedict was solemnly installed. Anastasius, Luitprand, Honoré of Autun, Godfrey of Viterbo, Albert of Stade, Matthew of Westminster, and the Fasciculus also lead us to the truth, but by a different road, in so far as they determine the length of Benedict III's pontificate to be two years, six months and ten days, which we have precisely between Sunday 29 September 855, the day of the said Benedict's enthronement, and Friday 8 April 858, the day of his death. Hardly anyone departs far from this reckoning except the Abbot of Ursperg, who cuts the thread of Leo's life only in the year 857, and within whose limits he encloses Benedict III's entire papacy, cutting off more than its just half. For Count Herman (although he begins in the year 856 and ends in 857, and so extends it to less than two full years) still limits it to two years, six months and nine days, one day fewer than the others; and Marianus, who takes the start of his prelacy from the year 857, grants him two years, six months and six days, cutting off 4 of the 10 days that are legitimately owed to him. Just so Florent of Worcester, who had begun the count of Leo IV's years wrongly at the year 853 (the very year in which Marianus claims he died), returns to himself in counting Benedict III's establishment in the year 855, and on this point agrees with the others.

units.la: Mais (pour ferrer plus estroittement le nœud de la preuve, & mettre la verité au dessus de toute contradiction) prenons les voix des auteurs tant du siecle de Benoist, que des plus voisins. Loup Abbé de Ferrieres, felicitant Benoist de sa promotion au Papat, use de ces termes : {1}Du temps de vostre devancier Leon de bienheureuse me-moire,
units.tr: But (to draw the knot of proof more tightly, and to place the truth beyond all contradiction) let us take the testimony of authors both from Benedict's own age and from those closest to it. Lupus, Abbot of Ferrières, congratulating Benedict on his promotion to the papacy, uses these words: {1} In the time of your predecessor Leo of blessed memory,

units.la: 1 Epist. 103. moire , ayant fait la fonction d'Ambassadeur à Rome, à laquelle (de par Dieu) vous presidez ; & ayant esté benignement accueilly & traitté par le mesme Prelat ; apres que la renommée a declaré que vous n'estes pas inferieur en religion, &c. j'ay osé (moy qui suis si petit) m'introduire par mes escrits en la connoissance de vostre sublimité. Notez qu'il tesmoigne avoir escrit si toft que le bruit l'a rendu certain de l'establissement de Benoist , & du rapport de ses vertus à celles de Leon ; & que son compliment tendant à relever l'estat de la reputation du nouveau Pape, en le faisant aller du pair en toutes choses avec son predecesseur, s'il l'avoit creu successeur de la pretendue Papesse , il n'auroit pas perdu l'occasion de tirer cette rencontre à la loüange,&estendre avec pompe sa comparaison dans un si vaste champ ; luy representant que comme il avoit fait revivre en sa personne les bonnes qualitez de Leon , il avoit effacé glorieusement l'opprobre de l'Eglise Romaine , honnie par la monstrueuse presidence d'une infame garse intruse apres sa mort au siege pontifical.
units.tr: 1 Epist. 103. memory, having performed the office of ambassador at Rome, over which (by God's grace) you preside, and having been kindly received and treated by the same Prelate; after report has declared that you are not inferior in religion, and so on, I have dared (I who am so small) to introduce myself by my writings to the knowledge of your sublimity. Note that he testifies to having written as soon as rumour made him certain of Benedict's establishment and of the likeness of his virtues to those of Leo. His compliment, which aims to raise the reputation of the new Pope by placing him on a level with his predecessor in all things, would not have let slip the chance to draw this coincidence to his praise, and to extend his comparison with pomp over so wide a field, if he had believed Benedict to be the successor of the supposed Papess. He represents to him that, as he had revived in his own person the good qualities of Leo, he had gloriously wiped away the disgrace of the Roman Church, dishonoured by the monstrous presidency of an infamous wench who intruded into the pontifical see after her death.

units.la: Le Pape Nicolas premier successeur de Benoist III, escrivant le 6 Decembre 866 au Concile de Soissons, dit que {1}le pontife Leon qui connoissoit les desseins du frere Hincmar, a esté foustrait de la lumiere de ce monde, & que Benoist de S. memoire, personnage Apostolique luy {1}ayant lors succedé en l'ordre du pontificat, derechef le mesme Reverend Hincmar a preparé les armes, & s'est glissé en cachette vers ce mesme souverain Prelat, comme vers une personne qui n'avoit pas fait l'espreuve de ses finesses: & luy a (au commencement mesme de sa consecration) persuadé de confirmer le Concile qui avoit esté autrefois assemblé au souhait d'un seul homme. Je ne fais pas force sur ce qu'il dit que Benoist a succedé à Leon: car comme S. Hierome dit de tous Evesques (en quelque siecle qu'ils vivent) qu'ils sont {2}Successeurs des Apostres, & Rome appelle encore aujourd'huy le Pape qui la gouverne Successeur de S. Pierre, martyrizé 1559 ans auparavant que Gregoire XV ait fait place à Vrbain VIII. & Guillaume Archevesque de Tyr (pour marquer le defaut de Raoul de Damfront possesseur du Patriarchat d'Antioche depuis l'an 1132) escrit {3}qu'il se monstroit plustost successeur d'Antiochus que de Pierre ou d'Ignace, decedez (comme chacun sçait) plusieurs siecles auparavant; & se porte soy mesme pour successeur de Guillaume, qu'il qualifie {4}expressement son predecesseur,
units.tr: Pope Nicholas I, successor of Benedict III, writing on 6 December 866 to the Council of Soissons, says that {1} the pontiff Leo, who knew the designs of brother Hincmar, has been removed from the light of this world, and that Benedict of holy memory, an Apostolic person, having then succeeded him in the order of the pontificate, again the same Reverend Hincmar prepared his arms, and slipped secretly to this same sovereign Prelate, as to one who had not made trial of his cunning, and persuaded him (at the very beginning of his consecration) to confirm the Council which had once been assembled at the wish of a single man. I do not press what he says, that Benedict succeeded Leo: for as St Jerome says of all bishops (in whatever century they live) that they are successors of the Apostles, and Rome still today calls the Pope who governs it successor of St Peter, who was martyred 1559 years before Gregory XV gave place to Urban VIII. And William, Archbishop of Tyre (to mark the defect of Raoul de Damfront, who possessed the Patriarchate of Antioch from the year 1132) writes that he showed himself successor of Antiochus rather than of Peter or Ignatius, who died (as everyone knows) many centuries earlier; and he presents himself as successor of William, whom he expressly describes {4} as his predecessor,

units.la: {1} Cum ei successif-fet. encore que Foucher, & Raoul, & Pierre, & Frederic ayent tenu le siege entre deux: on pourroit penser que Benoist troisiéme a esté successeur de Leon IV en la mesme façon.
units.tr: {1} Although Foucher, Raoul, Peter and Frederick each held the see in between, one might think that Benedict III succeeded Leo IV in the same way.

units.la: Et pour la mesme raison, je m'abstiens de preffer les lieux, où Nicolas (accouplant Leon avec Benoist) les appelle {1}les devanciers: où le Comte de Toul escrit aux Evesques de Bretagne, que Benoist a esté successeur de Leon; où Flodoard asseure {2}que l'action du Concile de Soiffons, addressée par Hincmar à l'Eglise Romaine, a esté corroborée par Benoist successeur de Leon; où Hugues Abbé de Fleuri donne le mesme titre à Benoist: où Photius, & Stylianus, & Metrophanes, reconnoissent que Benoist a esté apres Leon; & successeur apres luy au throne archisacerdotal. Façons de parler qui se trouvent aussi imitées {3}par Nicolas Maniacutius: pource qu'encore que ces expressions se puissent & doivent (selon l'intention des auteurs qui s'en sont servis) interpreter des successeurs immediats; elles peuvent facilement subsister avec la presupposition de ceux qui tiennent qu'il y a eu une Papesse intruse entre deux, veu que souvent elles se trouvent appliquées à des gens qui n'ont eu la succession cession l'un de l'autre que mediatement. ;
units.tr: For the same reason I refrain from pressing the passages where Nicolas, joining Leo with Benedict, calls them the predecessors; where the Count of Toul writes to the bishops of Brittany that Benedict was the successor of Leo; where Flodoard affirms {2}that the act of the Council of Soissons, addressed by Hincmar to the Roman Church, was confirmed by Benedict, successor of Leo; where Hugh, abbot of Fleury, gives Benedict the same title; and where Photius, Stylianus and Metrophanes acknowledge that Benedict came after Leo and was his successor on the archiepiscopal throne. Such ways of speaking are also imitated {3}by Nicolas Maniacutius. For although these expressions can and must (according to the intention of the authors who used them) be understood of immediate successors, they can easily stand alongside the supposition of those who hold that an intruding Papess came between the two, since they are often applied to men who received the succession from one another only mediately.

units.la: Ie ne puis non plus passer comme necessairement concluant , l'argument que Leo Allatius tire du livret qui avoit esté composé l'an 891 contre la memoire de Photius , sous le Papat de Formosus , & qu'il avoit luy mesme imprudemment confondu avec l'affiche attachée l'an 869 au porche de la grande Eglife de Constantinople , par les Legats de Rome , & des Sieges d'Orient,contre le mesme Photius. car encore que ce livret ayant compté 45 ans entre le commencement de Leon IV en 847 , & l'entrée de Formosus au Pontificat l'an 891 ; & partagé ces 45 ans entre 9 Papes , qu'il designe par leurs noms propres, à çavoir Leon IV, Benoist III, Nicolas I , Adrian II , Iean VIII , Marin I, Adrian III , Eftienne V , & Formose : face une seconde division des mesmes 45 ans en 2 parties,l'une d'onze ans,durant lesquels Photius seculier a esté anathematizé avec Gregoire de Syracuse par Leon, Benoist & Nicolas; & l'autre de trente quatre, durant lesquels le mesme desja promeu au Patriarchat , a esté fulminé de nouveau par Nicolas & ses successeurs jusques à Formose ; & par ces partitions (mesurant l'espace metoyen entre Sergius & Nicolas à la durée d'onze ans, qui appartiennent à Leon, Benoist, & audit Nicolas) il semble exclurre necessairement la pretendue Papes-se, que l'on a placée depuis entre Leon & Benoist; neantmoins il ne la peut exclurre en cas que l'on vueille donner lieu à l'hypothese de ceux qui luy ont destiné rang entre les Papes;pource que(convenant des onze ans entre Leon & Nicolas) ils en laissent moindre part à Leon & Benoist, pour faire reserve à laditte Papesse de celle qu'ils luy ont assignée.Ce qu'elle n'est pas comptée entre les 9 Papes, qui ont tenu le siege depuis l'an 847 jusques au 891 estant pris precisement,ne les blesse pas, attendu qu'ils reconnoissent qu'elle n'a eu que l'apparence de Pape, & que (bien loin de l'avoir esté en effect) elle n'a peu passer que pour Papesse. Et ce qu'il n'est fait aucune memoire d'excommunication lancée par elle contre Photius, ne peut estre allegué tout seul & à part à leur prejudice; pource qu'ayant posé (de la part de ceux qui l'ont reconnue) qu'elle a fulminé Photius à l'exemple de Leon, ils auroyent à repartir, que les Grecs adversaires de ce Prelat, n'eussent pas eu raison de faire mise d'un acte attenté contre luy, nul de tout droit; la puissance des clefs n'estant pas un heritage qui doive tomber en quenouille, de mesme que les Romains n'eussent pas eu sujet de se plaindre de leur omission, que personne de leur corps n'eust peu observer, sinon en renouvellant odieusement la memoire de l'opprobre de leur siege, & les mettant tous au rang de ceux aufquels S. Paul reprochoit {1} que leur gloire estoit en leur honte.
units.tr: Nor can I accept as necessarily conclusive the argument that Leo Allatius draws from the little book composed in 891 against the memory of Photius, under the papacy of Formosus, which he had himself imprudently confused with the placard fixed in 869 to the porch of the great church of Constantinople by the legates of Rome and of the Eastern sees against the same Photius. For although that little book counts 45 years between the beginning of Leo IV in 847 and the accession of Formosus to the pontificate in 891, and divides these 45 years among 9 Popes, whom it names individually, namely Leo IV, Benedict III, Nicholas I, Adrian II, John VIII, Marinus I, Adrian III, Stephen V and Formosus; and although it makes a second division of the same 45 years into two parts, one of eleven years, during which the secular Photius was anathematized along with Gregory of Syracuse by Leo, Benedict and Nicholas, and the other of thirty-four, during which the same man, already promoted to the patriarchate, was thundered against again by Nicholas and his successors down to Formosus; and although by these divisions (measuring the interval between Sergius and Nicholas as eleven years, which belong to Leo, Benedict and the said Nicholas) it seems necessarily to exclude the so-called Papess, whom people have since placed between Leo and Benedict, nevertheless it cannot exclude her if one wishes to give room to the hypothesis of those who have assigned her a rank among the Popes. For, granting the eleven years between Leo and Nicholas, they leave a smaller share to Leo and Benedict, so as to reserve for the said Papess the portion they have assigned to her. That she is not counted among the 9 Popes who held the see from 847 to 891, taken precisely, does not hurt them, since they acknowledge that she had only the appearance of a Pope, and that, far from having been one in fact, she could pass only as a Papess. And that no mention is made of any excommunication pronounced by her against Photius cannot be alleged alone and apart to their prejudice. For, having supposed (on the part of those who recognized her) that she fulminated against Photius after the example of Leo, they would have to reply that the Greek adversaries of that prelate would not have been right to make a point of an act attempted against him by one with no right at all, since the power of the keys is not an inheritance that should fall to the distaff; just as the Romans would not have had cause to complain of their omission, which no one of their body could have observed, except by odiously renewing the memory of the disgrace of their see and putting them all in the rank of those of whom St Paul reproached {1} that their glory was in their shame.

units.la: Aussi Allatius se rend ridicule, quand (apres avoir remarqué que l'Empereur Michel insultant sur la disgrace de Theodora sa mere, qu'il avoit depossedée l'an 855 au bout de 14 ans de gouvernement, tiroit de la vanité de ses ordures; & disoit de son bouffon; Theophile m'a esté fait Patriarche, & Photius à Cesar, & Ignace aux Chrestiens) il s'imagine que (si la Papesse eust jamais occupé le siege Romain) ce Prince desbordé & profane eust peu adjouster à sa raillerie, & Ieanne aux Romains. Car quiconque voudra soustenir le conte de cette Ieanne, aura moyen de fermer la bouche à ce dernier impugnateur par deux reparties, contraires de vray entr'elles, mais toutes deux cependant, destructives à divers egards, de son imagination. La premiere, que Michel a donné en effectà Rome l'atteinte que l'on luy attribue, & que le Pape Nicolas s'en est plaint, lors qu'il a respondu à ce jeune insolent , {1}qu'il avoit commencé sa lettre par injures & convices , & parlé injurieusement de l'Eglise Romaine , & escrit au des-avantage des Prelats du siege Apostolique ; & lors qu'il a remonstré à l'Archevesque Hincmar , que le mesme Prince luy avoit {2}addressé Michel son premier port'espée avec une epistre pleine d'injures. En effect qui empeschera les advocats de la pretendue Ieanne , d'appliquer les injures & detractions, dont Nicolas a fait plainte sans les exprimer , aux reproches que Michel avoit desgorgées , luy ramentevant (selon eux) l'intrusion de cette miserable au siege Papal? La seconde, incompatible avec la premiere , mais tres peremptoire , que Photius ayant esté elevé au {3}Patriarchat par le Cesar Bardas , le 25 Decembre 858 seulement , c'est à dire le 9 mois de la premiere année de Nicolas, & le 6 au plus de la douziesme d'Ignace, des-throné à l'occasion de Bardas , qui n'a esté salué Curopalate , & enfin Cesar{4} , qu'apres le second Concile assemblé contre Ignace dans l'Eglise des S. Apostres à Constantinople , au commencement de l'an 861 ; voire apres le retour des Legats de Rome, & le bruslement de S. Sophie, l'an 862,de mesme que Theophile n'a porté le titre de Patriarche des bouffons que sous le Cesareat de Bardas : Michel n'eust peu pour lors dire en verité, que Jeanne estoit le Patriarche des Romains, tout ainsi que Photius estoit celuy de Bardas. Veu que (selon la presupposition de ceux qui tiennent qu'elle a esté) elle estoit decedée des l'an 856, trois ans & plus devant l'intrusion de Photius, & six devant le Cesareat de Bardas. Et notez que voilà jusques où a peu porter la suffisance d'Allatius, le dernier de tous ceux qui ont disputé contre la Papesse pour Rome, & dans Rome mesmes.
units.tr: So Allatius makes himself ridiculous when, after remarking that the Emperor Michael, insulting the disgrace of his mother Theodora, whom he had deposed in 855 after fourteen years of government, drew vanity from his filthiness and said of his buffoon: Theophilus was made Patriarch for me, Photius Caesar, and Ignatius for the Christians, he imagines that (if the Papess had ever occupied the Roman see) this debauched and profane prince could have added to his mockery, and Joan for the Romans. For whoever wishes to maintain the story of this Joan will have a way of silencing this last assailant with two replies, contrary indeed to one another, yet both of them destructive, in different respects, of his imagining. The first is that Michael really did deliver to Rome the blow that is attributed to him, and that Pope Nicholas complained of it when he answered that young insolent, {1}that he had begun his letter with insults and reproaches, spoken injuriously of the Roman Church, and written to the disadvantage of the prelates of the apostolic see; and when he remonstrated with Archbishop Hincmar that the same Prince had {2}sent him Michael's first sword-belt together with a letter full of insults. Indeed, what would prevent the advocates of the so-called Joan from applying the insults and slanders of which Nicholas complained, without specifying them, to the reproaches that Michael had belched forth, reminding him (as they would have it) of the intrusion of this wretched woman into the papal see? The second reply, incompatible with the first but very decisive, is that Photius was raised to the patriarchate by the Caesar Bardas only on 25 December 858, that is to say in the ninth month of Nicholas's first year and at most the sixth month of Ignatius's twelfth year, when Ignatius had been deposed on Bardas's account; and Bardas was saluted as curopalates and finally as {4}Caesar only after the second council assembled against Ignatius in the church of the Holy Apostles at Constantinople, at the beginning of the year 861; indeed, only after the return of the Roman legates and the burning of St Sophia in 862. Just as Theophilus bore the title of Patriarch of the buffoons only under Bardas's Caesarate, Michael could not then have said in truth that Joan was the Patriarch of the Romans, just as Photius was Bardas's. Since (according to the supposition of those who hold that she existed) she had died in 856, three years and more before Photius's intrusion, and six before Bardas's Caesarate. And note that this is as far as the competence of Allatius has been able to carry, he being the last of all those who have disputed against the Papess on behalf of Rome, and within Rome itself.

units.la: Je ne veux en fin considerer que comme preuves subsidiaires, mais tres-foibles employées separement, les Catalogues que Hugues de Fleury, Honoré d'Austun & autres ont dressez des Papes, faisant suivre Benoist III immediatement apres Leon IV, & designant l'un & l'autre par des marques de nombres differentes, comme 100, & 101 apres S. Pierre, sans laisser entre deux aucune place pour la Papesse; d'autant que Marianus qui l'a fait le premier monter sur le theatre, employe les mesmes notes numerales à son exclusion : que ceux qui ont embraffé son advis, proteftent hautement que le nom de Ieanne ne fait point. de nombre ; & qu'en effect ayant esté (comme l'on pretend) Papesse, & non Pape ; elle n'a ni peu, ni deu tenir de rang dans le Catalogue des Papes, pour en allonger la lifte. Voila pourquoy je m'estonne que le Cardinal Baronius, & Poffevin, personnages doctes, & de profonde lecture, ayent fait si grande estime de l'erreur populaire publié sous le nom du Sr. de Remond, où rien de plus fort n'est mis en avant : & les choses qui euffent merité plus de consideration, ont esté ou entierement omises, ou ramenteües seulement en gros, & comme si l'auteur s'estoit proposé simplement de les enveloper dans la foule de quantité de pensées, ou superflues, ou mal convenables à celuy qui a voulu s'en dire le pere.
units.tr: Finally, I wish to consider the following only as subsidiary proofs, and very weak ones when used separately: the catalogues of popes drawn up by Hugh of Fleury, Honoré of Autun and others, which make Benedict III follow immediately after Leo IV and number each with a different figure, such as 100 and 101 after St Peter, leaving no place between the two for the Papess. Marianus, who first brought her onto the stage, uses the same numerical marks to exclude her. Those who have adopted his opinion declare loudly that the name of Joan does not make a number, and that, having been (as they allege) a Papess and not a Pope, she could neither hold a place in the catalogue of the popes nor lengthen the list. That is why I am astonished that Cardinal Baronius and Possevin, learned men of deep reading, have set such great store by the popular error published under the name of the Sieur de Remond, where nothing stronger is put forward. The matters that deserved more consideration have either been entirely omitted or touched on only in general, as if the author had meant simply to bury them in a crowd of thoughts that were either superfluous or ill-suited to the man who wished to call himself their father.

units.la: Mais je fonde ma preuve, 1. sur ce que le Pape Nicolas I dit {1}qu'alors que Leon a eftè retiré de la lumiere de ce monde, Benoist luy a fuccedé : & Ado, que {2}Leon mourant, Benoist a esté fubstitué. Et la Chronique de S. Bertin sur l'an 855, que Leon Prelat du fiege Apostolique eft decedé, & Benoist luy a succedé ; & Herman de mesme apres Anaftafe le Bibliothecaire, en la vie de Nicolas I, Leon eftant defunt.
units.tr: But I base my proof, (1) on the fact that Pope Nicholas I says that when Leo was taken from the light of this world, Benedict succeeded him; and Ado says that Leo dying, Benedict was substituted. The Chronicle of St Bertin, under the year 855, says that Leo, prelate of the Apostolic see, died, and Benedict succeeded him. Hermann likewise, following Anastasius the Librarian in the life of Nicholas I, says Leo being dead.

units.la: 2. Sur ce que le mesme Herman,& l'Abbé d'Vrsperg , & Matthieu de Weftmonftier , asseurent que Benoist a esté assis la mesme année en laquelle Leon est decedé, voire qu'Herman (en l'edition de 1613 à Francfort) parle de l'establissement de Benoist , avant que rien dire de la mort de Leon. Car voici les paroles sur l'année 856 de noftre Seigneur , Benoist III Pape 106 durant 2 ans, 6 mois , & 9 jours ; Leon Pape, Trogo, & Rabanus, & la Reine Hildegard[?] moururent. Car comme il est impossible que ces paroles soient vrayes , Leon mourant Benoist a esté substitué, si Ieanne a esté entre deux; ou que celles cy subsistent, lors que Leon a esté soustrait de la lumiere , Benoist luy a succedé, si (Ieanne ayant esté lors subrogée) Benoist n'a pris la place que deux ans, cinq mois, & quatre jours apres. Il y a encore moins d'apparence que Benoist ayt esté assis la mesme année, en laquelle Leon est mort, s'il n'a pas esté son successeur immediat ; & s'il a fallu qu'auparavant Ieanne ayt tenu le siege 2 ans, 5 mois, & 4 jours, comme Marianus a posé. Ie sçay bien qu'il y a de la confusion dans le discours d'Herman , veu que Leon est decedé le 17 Juillet 855[?] , & Trogo ou Dreux de Metz le 8 Novembre suivant , & Rabanus le 4 Fevrier 856, quoy que c'en foit moins de 7 mois de temps apres les autres. Mais cela n'altere en rien la force de la preuve, qui date l'eftabliffement de Benoist,de l'année mefme en laquelle Leon eft mort.
units.tr: (2) The same Hermann, the Abbot of Ursperg and Matthew of Westminster assert that Benedict was seated in the very year in which Leo died. Hermann indeed (in the edition of 1613 at Frankfurt) speaks of Benedict's establishment before saying anything about Leo's death. Here are his words for the year 856 of our Lord: Benedict III, Pope 106, for 2 years, 6 months and 9 days; Leo, Pope, Drogo and Rabanus, and Queen Hildegard[?] died. If Joan came between the two, these words cannot be true, Leo dying, Benedict was substituted. Nor can these stand, when Leo was taken from the light, Benedict succeeded him, if (Joan having been put in then) Benedict took the place only two years, five months and four days later. There is still less likelihood that Benedict was seated in the same year in which Leo died, if he was not his immediate successor, and if Joan had to hold the see for 2 years, 5 months and 4 days before him, as Marianus has laid down. I am well aware that there is confusion in Hermann's account, since Leo died on 17 July 855[?], Drogo of Metz on 8 November following, and Rabanus on 4 February 856, although these dates are less than seven months apart. But this does not in any way weaken the force of the proof, which dates Benedict's establishment to the very year in which Leo died.

units.la: 3. Ie preffe cette claufe de l'Epiftre de Nicolas au Concile de Soiffons, Hincmar a perfuadé à Benoist au commencement mesme de sa confecration de confirmer le Concile, où son titre Archiepiscopal luy avoit esté affermi. Car par la response d'Hincmar à Nicolas, il conste que cette confirmation s'est faitte l'année mesme de la mort de Leon. Avec cette lettre (dit il){1} & avec la legation de l'Empereur (Lothaire) avec lettres dont j'ay une copie, touchant la demande des Evesques & mes autres demandes, j'ay addressé par le susdit venerable Evesque [ Pierre d'Arezzo ] mes messagers à Rome,{2} aufquels en chemin vint nouvelle de la mort du Pape Leon. Or arrivans à Rome avec lesdites lettres, & lesdits Evesques (Pierre{3} de Spoleto,& Pierre d'Arezzo) intervenans;Monsieur Benoist de nom, & de grace, (ce que vous m'estes) m'a addressé de la son privilege. Voila donc les messagers d'Hincmar envoyez du vivant de Lothaire, decedé le 29 Septembre 855; & avant que la France eust reçeu aucun advis de la mort de Leon, arrivée le 17 Iuillet precedent. Entre Rheims & Rome (distans au plus de 300 lieues, quelque chemin que l'on prene) ces mesmes messagers apprenent que celuy vers lequel ils avoient esté depeschez estoit hors du monde ; & neantmoins poursuivent leur voyage, à leur arrivée dans Rome, ils trouvent Benoist III establi. Dira t'on (pour conserver l'honneur de la fable) qu'ils se font promenez deçà & delà les Alpes 2 ans & demi, attendant que le terme de Ieanne intruse (comme on pretend) en la place de Leon, ait esté expiré? la course auroit esté belle, mais un peu longue.
units.tr: (3) I press this clause of Nicholas' letter to the Council of Soissons: Hincmar persuaded Benedict, at the very beginning of his consecration, to confirm the Council, by which his archiepiscopal title had been confirmed. From Hincmar's reply to Nicholas it is clear that this confirmation was made in the very year of Leo's death. With this letter (he says){1} and with the legation of the Emperor (Lothair), with letters of which I have a copy, concerning the request of the bishops and my other requests, I sent my messengers to Rome{2} through the aforesaid venerable bishop [Peter of Arezzo]. On the way news came to them of the death of Pope Leo. Arriving at Rome with the said letters, and with the said bishops (Peter{3} of Spoleto and Peter of Arezzo) interceding, Lord Benedict, by name and by grace (what you are to me), sent me from there his privilege. So here are Hincmar's messengers, sent during the lifetime of Lothair, who died on 29 September 855, and before France had received any word of Leo's death, which occurred on the previous 17 July. Between Reims and Rome (at most 300 leagues apart, whatever road one takes), these same messengers learn that the man to whom they had been dispatched was out of the world; yet they continue their journey, and on arriving at Rome they find Benedict III established. Will one say, to preserve the honour of the fable, that they wandered this way and that across the Alps for two and a half years, waiting for the term of the intruder Joan (as they allege) in Leo's place to expire? The journey would have been a fine one, but rather long.

units.la: 4. l'infiste sur les paroles d'Anastase qui font formelles. Lors (dit il) {1} que le Prelat Leon soustrait de cette lumiere fut {2} abbatu, incontinent tout le Clergé de ce siege Romain protegé, & tous les principaux, & tout le Senat, & le peuple s'assemblerent, & d'un effort {3} publierent Pape Benoist, le Clergé & tous les principaux composans le decret, le fortifierent de leurs signatures propres ; & (comme l'ancienne coustume requiert) l'envoyerent aux tres-invincibles Augustes Lothaire & Louys. Autant en dit Luitprand en propres termes. Mesmes Sigebert en convient, qui escrit tresveritablement (quoy que hors de son lieu à sçavoir sur l'année 854) Benoist presfide le cent deuxiéme sur l'Eglise Romaine.Cettuycy ayant esté deposé par la confpiration des malins, Anastase envahit la Prelature. Mais Anastase ayant esté mis bas par les legats de l'Empereur Lothaire, & poussé en prison, Benoist fut honorablement remis en sa place. Lothaire vivoit donc encore, & puis qu'il est (comme nous avons demonstré) decedé le Dimanche 29 Septemb. 855; il faut de toute necessité que ce grabuge soit arrivé dans le 3 mois d'apres la mort de Leon.
units.tr: (4) I insist on the words of Anastasius, which are formal. Then (he says), when the prelate Leo was taken from this light and struck down, at once the whole clergy of this Roman see, protected, and all the principal men, and the Senate and people assembled, and with one effort proclaimed Benedict pope. The clergy and all the principal men, composing the decree, strengthened it with their own signatures, and (as ancient custom requires) sent it to the most invincible Augusti, Lothair and Louis. Luitprand says the same in the same terms. Even Sigebert agrees, who writes very truly (though out of its place, under the year 854): Benedict presided over the Roman Church as the hundred and second. He having been deposed by the conspiracy of the wicked, Anastasius seized the prelacy. But Anastasius having been cast down by the legates of the Emperor Lothair and thrust into prison, Benedict was honourably restored to his place. Lothair therefore was still alive; and since he died (as we have demonstrated) on Sunday, 29 September 855, this upheaval must necessarily have happened within three months after Leo's death.

units.la: Tirons donc (hardiment & sans crainte de nous mesprendre) le detail de tout le schisme, du discours d'Anastase le Bibliothecaire qui le represente exactement, & jusques à la remarque des plus menües particularitez. Nicolas {1}Evesque d'Alagna,& Mercure maistre de la gendarmerie, deputez des Romains vers les Empereurs Lothaire & Louys, s'abouchent en chemin avec Arsenius {2}Evesque d'Agobio; & braffent de faire deposer Benoist, & subroger en son lieu ce mesme Anastase preftre Cardinal du titre de S. Marcel,qui avoit(comme deserteur de son miniftere) esté depose par Leon IV, & son Concile assemblé dans Rome le 8 Decemb. 853; c'est à dire au mesme temps auquel Marianus veut que
units.tr: Let us therefore take the full account of the whole schism, boldly and without fear of going wrong, from the narrative of Anastasius the librarian, who reports it exactly and notes even the smallest details. Nicholas {1}bishop of Alagna and Mercury, master of the cavalry, deputies of the Romans sent to the Emperors Lothair and Louis, meet Arsenius {2}bishop of Agobio on the way. They plan to depose Benoist and to put in his place that same Anastasius, priest and cardinal of the title of St Marcellus, who had been deposed by Leo IV and his council assembled at Rome on 8 December 853, as a deserter of his ministry. That was the very time at which Marianus wants

units.la: ᵛ[?] Ils ont tous 2 assisté au mesme Concile, & Radoald (envoyé depuis, a sçavoir l'an 863, Legat a Constantinople avec Zacharie d'Alagna successeur de Nicolas) ayant passé sa commission l'an 861, fut deposé par Nicolas I l'an 862, apres son retour.
units.tr: They all took part in the same council, and Radoald, who was sent later, in 863, as legate to Constantinople with Zacharias of Alagna, Nicholas's successor, having surrendered his commission in 861, was deposed by Nicholas I in 862 after his return.

units.la: ⁴ Roma que fa Ieanne ayt commencé de tenir le fiege. Apres voyant que les Commissaires de l'Empereur Louys avoient ordre exprez de se rendre à Rome, ils donnent advis aux Romains, d'envoyer au devant ; & les Romains despeschent Radoald{1} & Agathon Evesques de Porto & de Todi, qui s'avancent jusques à Horta à 40 miles de Rome, prennent le party d'Anastafe contre Benoist ; font emprisonner{2} George & Majo Evesques de Bomarzo & de Piperno ; mandent le peuple pour le faire acheminer jusques au delà de Ponte Mole ; & font (apres leur arrivée) arrester Adrian,{3} Gratian, & Theodore, du corps de la ville, & du Clergé Romain. Anastafe de son costé porté par eux (s'estant violemment faisi du Palais Patriarchal de Latran) commande à 4 Romain, Evesque de Bagnarea, de deposseder Benoist, qu'il donne (le Samedy 21 Septembre) en garde à Iean & à Adrian, deposez quelque temps auparavant du Presbyterat par Leon I V : le Lundy suivant 23 du mesme mois, toute la faction s'affemble dans la paroisse dite Emiliane, où se trouvent les Commissaires Imperiaux, qui ne prennent nullement en paye ce que les
units.tr: ⁴ Rome, that Joan began to hold the see. Afterwards, seeing that the commissioners of the Emperor Louis had express orders to make for Rome, they gave notice to the Romans to send out to meet them. The Romans dispatched Radoald and Agathon, bishops of Porto and Todi, who advanced as far as Horta, forty miles from Rome, took the side of Anastasius against Benedict, had George and Majus, bishops of Bomarzo and Piperno, thrown into prison, summoned the people to escort them as far as beyond Ponte Mole, and, after their arrival, had Adrian, Gratian and Theodore arrested, men of the city and of the Roman clergy. Anastasius, for his part, carried along by them (having violently seized the Patriarchal Palace of the Lateran), ordered Forty, bishop of Bagnarea, to depose Benedict. On Saturday 21 September he handed Benedict into the custody of John and Adrian, who had been deposed from the presbyterate some time before by Leo IV. On the following Monday, 23 of the same month, the whole faction assembled in the parish called Emiliane, where the imperial commissioners were present; they by no means accepted as sufficient the excuses which the bishops of Ostia and Albano put forward in their defence. On Tuesday 24 the whole people, gathered in the Basilica of Constantine, which is the cathedral of Rome, demanded the restoration of Benedict with such unanimous consent and vehement insistence that the deputies of the Emperor Louis gave way and drove Anastasius the antipope out of the Patriarchate. Following this, a three-day fast was proclaimed in the basilica called ad praesepe, now S. Maria Maggiore, for Wednesday, Thursday and Friday, 25, 26 and 27 September. On Saturday 28 they all with one accord brought Benedict back to the Patriarchate of the Lateran; and on Sunday 29, which was (according to Regino and the other authorities cited above) the very day of the death of the Emperor Lothar, or, according to the Chronicle of S. Bertin, the day after, Ado, who says that Leo, dying, Benedict was substituted, adds that nevertheless (Lothar being already dead) at break of day they led him to the Church of S. Peter, where he was consecrated.

units.la: le Duc Gregoire ; de Gratian superintendant du palais, parle de Leon I V : Theodore estoit Concierge. [?]n avoit succedé à Leon, l'un des 67 Evesques du Concile 853. les Evefques d'Oftia {1} & d'Albano alleguent pour leur defcharge. Le Mardy 24 tout le peuple assemblé dans la Basilique Constantienne,qui est la Cathedrale deRome, demande le restablissement de Benoist avec un si grand consentement, & forte instance, que les Deputez de l'Empereur Louys acquiescent, & chassent Anastase l' Antipape du Patriarchat. En suitte de quoy, un jusne de trois jours ayant esté indit en la Basilique intitulée ad præsepe,maintenant S. Marie Majour, pour les Mercredy, Ieudy, & Vendredy 25, 26, & 27 Septembre, le Samedy 28, tous d'un accord ramenent Benoist au Patriarchat de Latran ; & le Dimanche 29 , qui estoit (selon Regino , & les autres cottez cy dessus) le jour propre de la mort de l'Empereur Lothaire, ou selon la Chronique de S. Bertin, le lendemain: à cause de quoy Ado qui dit que Leon mourant , Benoist fut subftitué, adjoufte , {2} toutesfois (Lothaire estant desja defunct) {3} des la pointe du jour , le conduisent en l'Eglise de S. Pierre, là où il est sacré.
units.tr: Duke Gregory; Gratian, superintendent of the palace, speaks of Leo IV; Theodore was the doorkeeper. [?]n had succeeded Leo, one of the 67 bishops of the Council of 853. The bishops of Ostia {1} and Albano allege in their defence. On the 24th the whole people, assembled in the Basilica of Constantine, which is the cathedral of Rome, demanded the restoration of Benedict with such great consent and forceful insistence that the deputies of the Emperor Louis acquiesced and drove Anastasius the antipope out of the Patriarchate. Following this, a fast of three days having been appointed in the basilica entitled ad praesepe, now S. Maria Maggiore, for Wednesday, Thursday and Friday, 25, 26 and 27 September, on Saturday 28 they all in agreement brought Benedict back to the Patriarchate of the Lateran; and on Sunday 29, which was (according to Regino and the other authorities cited above) the very day of the death of the Emperor Lothar, or according to the Chronicle of S. Bertin, the day after, Leo dying, Benedict was substituted, Ado adds, {2} nevertheless (Lothar being already dead) {3} at break of day, they led him to the Church of S. Peter, where he was consecrated.

units.la: Qui jamais ouït d'histoire plus circonstanciée, & de circonstances plus infaillibles , veu que les lieux, & les personnes, & les temps, & les caractères des jours, & les momens mesmes sont rapportez si distinctement, qu'il ne se peut rien au monde de plus exprez? Pourroit il bien venir en l'esprit d'aucun de garder encor le moindre ombrage contre ce recit, apres avoir attentivement consideré qu'il est confirmé au fonds par le Concile Romain de l'an 853, par Nicolas I, par Ado, par Hincmar, par les Annales de S. Bertin, par Luitprand, & par Sigebert; c'est à dire par l'un des auteurs ausquels on attribue la principale defence du Roman de la Papesse? Voilà donc Benoist III (apres une traverse d'environ six semaines) en possession paisible du siege de Leon IV, dés le Dimanche 29 Septembre 855: & presques en mesme temps il confirme le Decret du Concile de Soissons, touchant l'establissement d'Hincmar en l'Archevesché de Rheims, par une lettre qui se trouve en son entier jusqu'aujourd'huy. Quelques 3 mois apres un grand desbordement du Tibre se fait dans Rome, principalement le 6 Janvier 856, & Anastase le Bibliothecaire asseure qu'il arriva dans le cinquiesme mois d'apres la consecration de Benoist, pource que son Pontificat avoit entamé les mois de Septembre & Janvier, & occupé les trois autres interjacens, entierement. En la mesme année 856 Benoist s'employe à l'affermissement de la paix entre l'Empereur Louys II, Lothaire Roy de Lorraine, & Charles Roy de Provence, enfans de l'Empereur Lothaire ; & de cela il nous donne luy mesme le certificat en sa 2 epistre,escrite au sujet du Comte Hubert Abbé de Luxueil frere de Thietberge femme du Roy Lothaire. L'onzième May de la 8 année {1}du Consulat de l'Empereur Louys, & durant l'indiction 5, (c'est à dire l'an 857) il ottroye & fait par Megistus Evesque d'Ostia (mentionné au Concile tenu le 8 Decemb. 853 à Rome, par Leon IV) expedier au monastere de S.Denys,sa charte inserée tout du long par F. Iacques Doublet en son histoire de S.Denys. En fin (decedant le Vendredy 8 Auril 858) il laisse sa place à Nicolas I, sacré le Dimanche 24 du mesme mois.
units.tr: Who has ever heard of a more detailed history, and of circumstances more trustworthy, since the places, the persons, the times, the marks of the days and even the moments are reported so distinctly that nothing in the world could be more precise? Could it possibly enter anyone's mind to still harbour the least suspicion against this account, after carefully considering that it is confirmed in substance by the Roman Council of 853, by Nicholas I, by Ado, by Hincmar, by the Annals of S. Bertin, by Luitprand and by Sigebert; that is to say, by some of the authors to whom the principal defence of the romance of the Papess is attributed?
