Here then is Benedict III, after a disturbance of about six weeks, in peaceful possession of the see of Leo IV from Sunday 29 September 855; and almost at the same time he confirmed the decree of the Council of Soissons concerning the installation of Hincmar in the archbishopric of Reims, by a letter which survives in its entirety to this day. Some three months later a great flooding of the Tiber occurred in Rome, principally on 6 January 856, and Anastasius the librarian assures us that it happened in the fifth month after the consecration of Benedict, because his pontificate had begun in September and January and had occupied the three intervening months entirely. In the same year, 856, Benedict worked to secure peace between the Emperor Louis II, Lothar King of Lorraine and Charles King of Provence, sons of the Emperor Lothar; and of this he himself gives us the certificate in his 2 epistle, written concerning Count Hubert, abbot of Luxeuil, brother of Theutberga, wife of King Lothar. On the eleventh of May in the eighth year {1} of the consulship of the Emperor Louis, and during the fifth indiction (that is, the year 857), he granted, and caused to be dispatched through Megistus, bishop of Ostia (mentioned at the council held on 8 December 853 in Rome under Leo IV), his charter for the monastery of S. Denis, inserted in full by Fr. Jacques Doublet in his history of S. Denis. Finally, dying on Friday 8 April 858, he left his place to Nicholas I, consecrated on Sunday 24 of the same month.

units.la: En quelle cachette nous pourra t'on dire qu'ayent esté lors, & le titre, & le siege , & la puissance de la pretendue Papesse ? & nous obligera t'on (pour l'apprendre au vray) à prendre langue de Godefroy de Viterbe escrivain posterieur de 328 ans, comme ayant escrit l'an 1186; & avec tant d'estourdissement d'esprit, qu'il n'a point fait de scrupule de se charger de deux Papes imaginaires, à sçavoir Paul & Estienne, qu'il place (de son autorité) entre Benoist & Nicolas, avec un partage si liberal,que le premier a pour son assignat, 10 ans & 2 mois de siege : & le deuxiéme (apres un interregne d'un an) quatre ans prefix ; afin que Nicolas I & les autres suivans ayent le plaisir de faire une reculée de 15 ans. Ou voudra t'on nous donner pour tablature d'histoire,les caprices de la Compilation Chronologique, qui copie ce que Godefroy a resvé touchant son Paul,& la durée de son Pontificat pretendu ; nonobstant que d'une part elle ayt fait monter Benoist III sur le siege l'an 856,avec asseurance de deux ans de seance, qui eussent deu expirer, soit avec l'an 857, soit au commencement de l'an 858 ; & de l'autre, commencé le Papat de Nicolas I à l'an 860 ; de mesme que si (pour ruiner de sa main propre ses propres suppositions) elle se fust obligée à escrire sur les dix années de Paul, pour neant ?
units.tr: In what hiding place can we say that the title, the see and the power of the so-called Papess were then? And are we to be obliged (to learn the truth) to take our information from Godfrey of Viterbo, a writer 328 years later, since he wrote in 1186, and with such a confusion of mind that he has not scrupled to insert two imaginary popes, namely Paul and Stephen, whom he places (on his own authority) between Benoist and Nicholas, with so generous a distribution that the first receives as his allotment 10 years and 2 months of the see, and the second (after an interregnum of a year) a fixed four years; so that Nicholas I and the later popes may have the pleasure of a fifteen-year postponement? Or shall we be given, as a table of history, the whims of the Chronological Compilation, which copies what Godfrey dreamed about his Paul and the length of his supposed pontificate; although on the one hand it sets Benoist III on the see in the year 856, with the assurance of two years in office, which should have expired either in the year 857 or at the beginning of 858, and on the other hand it begins the papacy of Nicholas I in the year 860, just as if (in order to ruin its own suppositions with its own hand) it had bound itself to write off the ten years of Paul for nothing?

units.la: Iusqu'icy nous avons donné la preuve directe de la verité du fait qui estoit en question ; estimant qu'il n'eust pas esté à propos de monstrer d'abord , que nous pouvions à bon droit trouver à redire au discours de Marianus , & que si nous eussions pensé , ou en demeurer là , ou commencer par là ; nous eussions aisement induit ceux qui se tiennent à son rapport, à nous opposer, qu'il sera, & a tousjours esté, trop plus aisé d'alleguer mille inconveniens, que de bien resoudre une seule difficulté. Mais apres avoir entierement levé celle que l'on nous pouvoit faire en sa faveur, & demonstré à l'œil ce que nous avions entrepris de verifier, il est juste que nous donnions un trait de plume à l'examen de son Roman, & rendions palpable à ceux qui veulent prendre pied sur un si mauvais fonds, qu'il leur en laisse fort peu de moyen.
units.tr: Hitherto we have given the direct proof of the truth of the fact in question. We judged it unwise to show first that we could fairly object to Marianus's account. Had we thought of doing so at the start, or of stopping there, we would have easily led those who rely on his report to answer us that it is, and always has been, much easier to allege a thousand inconveniences than to resolve a single difficulty. But now that we have entirely removed the objections that could be raised in his favour, and have demonstrated plainly what we undertook to verify, it is right that we give a few strokes of the pen to an examination of his romance, and make clear to those who wish to take their stand on so bad a foundation that it leaves them very little room.

units.la: Sur l'année 844 de nostre Seigneur, qui estoit (selon son compte) la quatriesme année de l'Empereur Lothaire, il fait cette remarque : Sergius Pape 101 apres S. Pierre a tenu le siege 3 ans : & sur la 847 qui estoit la troisieme de Lothaire, cette autre: Otgier Archevesque de Mayence meurt, Rabanus Abbé de Fulde luy succeda. Hattho est fait Abbé ; Sergius Pape mourut, & à cettuy-cy Leon succeda durant 8 ans. On pourroit presumer qu'il s'est contenté des nombres ronds sans s'engager à faire des menues remarques, des mois & jours que Sergius II & Leon IV ont vescu par dessus les années qu'il leur assigne ; le premier ayant esté Pape, trois ans, un mois, & deux jours, depuis le Dimanche 10 Febvrier 844, jusques au Mardy 12 Auril 847: & le second ayant tenu le siege apres luy, 8 ans, 3 mois, & 5 jours, commençans au Mardy 12 Auril 847, & finissans au Mercredy 17 Juillet 855. Mais si telle avoit esté sa pensée, comment luy seroit il arrivé de compter si precisement les mois & les jours, tant de sa Jeanne, que des antecedens, comme Estienne I I, Leon I I I, Estienne I V, Eugene &c. & des suivans comme Benoist I I I, & Nicolas I ? Il y a donc grande apparence, qu'il a creu devoir couper le Papat de Leon I V au bout des 8 années precisement; & je veux (pour m'accommoder à son compte) presupposer qu'il ne les a pas passées d'un moment: mais cela mesme estant pris pour un fondement arresté, qui ne void que la 8 des années commencées soit au Mardy 12 Auril 847, comme la verité requiert, soit au Jeudy 10 Febvrier de la mesme année selon que Marianus adjuste son calcul, se devoit terminer à pareils jours dans l'an 855? & partant qu'il avoit la berluë quand sur l'an 853, qui estoit le 13 de Lothaire, & le 7 de Leon I V, il a escrit le Pape Leon mourut le 1 Aoust. A cettuicy succeda Jeanne femme , 2 ans , 5 mois , & 4 jours ? Certes il ne peut nullement estre vray ( selon son hypothese propre ) que le Pape Leon soit mort au 1 Aoust , s'il a tenu le siege 8 ans prefix à commencer du 10Febvrier;ni que (s'il est mort le 1 Aoust) il ayt peu posseder le Papat 8 ans precisement ; ni en fin que (s'il est mort dans l'an 853 ) il ayt seulement entamé sa huitiéme année , qui ne devoit commencer qu'en Fevrier, ou en Auril de l'an 854; & quand on aura voulu prendre les jets pour appurer le compte de sa vie , on trouvera que le 1 Aoust 853 estoit encore du 4 mois de sa 7 année. D'ailleurs qu'il soit impossible de rapporter sa mort au 1 Aoust 853 ; appert , parce que plus de 4 mois apres il assembla dans Rome un Concile de 67 Evesques , où furent dressez 42 Canons , dont le sommaire a esté inseré par Luitprand dans son recueil de la vie des Papes ; & Anastase prestre Cardinal du titre de S. Marcel deserteur de sa charge , depose par sentence , qui se trouve dans les Tomes des Conciles sous ce titre , Regnans nos Seigneurs trefpieux, perpetuels Augustes , Lothaire couronné de Dieu , pacifique & grand Empereur en sa 37 année , & Louys couronné de Dieu son fils nouvel Empereur en sa 5 année , au mois de
units.tr: For the year 844 of our Lord, which was (by his reckoning) the fourth year of the Emperor Lothair, he makes this remark: Pope Sergius, the 101st after St Peter, held the see for 3 years. And for 847, the third year of Lothair, this other: Otgar, Archbishop of Mainz, dies; Rabanus, Abbot of Fulda, succeeded him. Hatto is made Abbot; Pope Sergius died, and Leo succeeded him for 8 years. One might suppose that he was content with round numbers and did not engage himself to make minor remarks about the months and days by which Sergius II and Leo IV lived beyond the years he assigns them. The first was Pope three years, one month and two days, from Sunday 10 February 844 until Tuesday 12 April 847. The second, who held the see after him, held it 8 years, 3 months and 5 days, beginning on Tuesday 12 April 847 and ending on Wednesday 17 July 855. But if this had been his thought, how could it have happened that he counted so precisely the months and days, both of his Joan and of her predecessors, such as Stephen II, Leo III, Stephen IV, Eugenius, etc., and of her successors, such as Benedict III and Nicholas I? There is therefore great likelihood that he thought fit to end Leo IV's pontificate exactly at the end of 8 years. And I will (to accommodate myself to his reckoning) presuppose that he did not exceed them by a single moment. But even granting this as a fixed foundation, does it not follow that, whether the 8th year began on Tuesday 12 April 847, as the truth requires, or on Thursday 10 February of the same year, as Marianus adjusts his calculation, it should have ended on the same days in the year 855? And therefore he was mistaken when, under the year 853, which was the 13th of Lothair and the 7th of Leo IV, he wrote: Pope Leo died on 1 August. Joan, a woman, succeeded him, for 2 years, 5 months and 4 days? Certainly, according to his own hypothesis, it cannot possibly be true that Pope Leo died on 1 August, if he held the see for 8 years fixed to begin from 10 February. Nor can it be that, if he died on 1 August, he could have held the papacy for precisely 8 years. And finally, if he died in the year 853, he would only have entered his eighth year, which was not to begin until February or April of 854. And if one wishes to take the counts to settle the reckoning of his life, one will find that 1 August 853 was still in the 4th month of his 7th year. Moreover, that it is impossible to place his death on 1 August 853 is clear, because more than four months later he assembled in Rome a council of 67 bishops, where 42 canons were drawn up, whose summary Luitprand inserted in his collection of the lives of the Popes. And Anastasius, priest and cardinal of the title of St Marcellus, who had deserted his office, was deposed by a sentence which is found in the volumes of the Councils under this title: Our most pious lords, perpetual Augusti, Lothair crowned by God, peaceful and great Emperor in his 37th year, and Louis crowned by God, his son, the new Emperor in his 5th year, in the month of

units.la: Lothaire fut associé à l'empire par Louys le debonnaire son pere l'an 817, comme remarque Eginhard: Et Louys son fils par luy mesme l'an 849 Decembre, au 8 jour, indiction seconde commençant en la cité neuve dont le nom est Leonienne, c'est à dire(selon le langage d'à present) le Bourg S. Pierre. L'an 8 de son Pontificat, indiction 2 courant, c'est à dire l'an 854 qui devoit (selon le compte de Marianus) commencer la seconde année de sa Papesse, Leon (comme remarque Anastase) bastit la ville de Leopoli à 12 milles de Città Vecchia di Cincelle. Et qu'il ayt prolongé sa vie jusques dans la neufviéme année de son Pontificat, qui se commencoit au 12 d'Auril 855 ; le mesme Anastase le certifie, lors qu'il raconte que Daniel maistre de la milice accusa le Pape de trahison avec Gratian aussi maistre de la milice, & superintendant de la ville & du Palais, & autres Romains: ce qui donna occasion à l'Empereur Louys de se transporter en personne sur les lieux pour ouïr les justifications des accusez, apres lesquelles il se retira, & non beaucoup de jours apres le Pape s'endormit au Seigneur le 17 Juillet.
units.tr: Lothair was associated in the empire by his father Louis the Debonair in the year 817, as Eginhard remarks. And Louis his son was associated by Lothair himself in the year 849, December, on the 8th day, second indiction, beginning in the new city whose name is Leonine, that is (in today's language) the Borgo of St Peter. In the 8th year of his pontificate, indiction 2 running, that is the year 854, which was to begin (according to Marianus's reckoning) the second year of his Papess, Leo (as Anastasius remarks) built the town of Leopoli 12 miles from Città Vecchia di Cincelle. And that he prolonged his life into the ninth year of his pontificate, which began on 12 April 855, the same Anastasius certifies, when he relates that Daniel, master of the militia, accused the Pope of treason together with Gratian, also master of the militia, and superintendent of the city and the Palace, and other Romans. This gave occasion to the Emperor Louis to go in person to the place to hear the justifications of the accused. After these he withdrew, and not many days later the Pope fell asleep in the Lord on 17 July.

units.la: Par ce moyen il est evident, qu'en depit de l'Arithmetique de Marianus, il est absolument necessaire que tout le temps qu'il a assigné à sa Ieanne, s'eclipse des années 853 & 854. Posons toutesfois (pour complaire à ceux qui ont un fort prejugé en faveur de sa suffisance & bonne foy) que la ditte Ieanne ayt (comme il suppose) pris la place de Leon, entre le 1 Aoust, & la fin de l'année 853: puis qu'il ne luy accorde que 2 ans, 5 mois, & 4 jours de siege, ne s'oblige t'il pas à luy faire prendre congé de la compagnie des le commencement de l'an 856; & dire qu'il y ayt eu depuis la mort de Leon un interregne de cinq mois entiers, chose non seulement inouïe, mais diametralement contraire au sentiment de tous les auteurs qui ont escrit, avec quelque lumiere de raison,touchant la vie tant de ce Pape que de ses successeurs? De quoy s'est donc advisé Marianus, lors qu'il a remis le Pape Benoist III à l'an 857? avoit il encor à feindre un second interregne de fix mois,& par delà, apres la mort de la pretendue Papesse, pour donner à Rome un entier loisir d'en porter le dueil? Et cela mesme n'est il pas totalement incompatible avec les depositions d'Ado, Nicolas I, Hincmar, Anastase, Luitprand, & Sigebert, attestans que Benoist est entré en charge au mesme temps que l'Empereur Lothaire est mort; c'est à dire l'an 855?
units.tr: By this means it is evident that, despite Marianus's arithmetic, it is absolutely necessary that the whole time he has assigned to his Joan be eclipsed by the years 853 and 854. Nevertheless, let us suppose (to please those who hold a strong prejudice in favour of his competence and good faith) that the said Joan took, as he supposes, the place of Leo between 1 August and the end of the year 853. Since he grants her only 2 years, 5 months and 4 days of the see, is he not obliged to have her take leave of company at the beginning of the year 856, and to say that there was after Leo's death an interregnum of five entire months? This is not only unheard of, but diametrically opposed to the opinion of all the authors who have written, with some light of reason, concerning the lives both of this Pope and of his successors. What, then, did Marianus think of when he placed Pope Benedict III in the year 857? Did he still need to feign a second interregnum of six months, and beyond that, after the death of the supposed Papess, to give Rome full leisure to mourn her? And is this itself not totally incompatible with the testimonies of Ado, Nicholas I, Hincmar, Anastasius, Luitprand and Sigebert, who attest that Benedict entered office at the very time when the Emperor Lothair died, that is to say in the year 855?

units.la: Il adjoufte apres Regino fur l'an 855, qui eftoit le 15 & dernier de Lothaire l'Empereur ayant convoqué les premiers du royaume, a divisé l'empire entre ses fils ; & baillé l'Italie à Louys, & l'a fait appeller de son nom Empereur. A Lothaire il a concedé le Royaume qui est appellé de son nom. Mais à Charles le plus jeune d'entr'eux il a recommandé la Provence. Ayant fait cette disposition, il a laissé le siecle, & est venu au monastere de Prom, & la mesme année est mort le 29 Septembre, apres qu'il a pris l'habit de la sainte conversation des Moines. Ie demeure d'accord du partage fait par Lothaire entre ses enfans, de sa reclusion à Prom, & de son trespas qui a suivi incontinent apres. Mais je soustiens qu'auparavant sa mort Benoist III avoit esté elevé en la place de Leon IV par les Romains ; puis que le Decret de son election avoit esté envoyé à Lothaire, comme Anastase & Luitprand remarquent specifiquement : que les messagers d'Hincmar, qui s'acheminoient à Rome avec les Ambassadeurs du mesme Lothaire, y trouverent à leur arrivée Benoist seant en la place de Leon : & que les Ambassadeurs de Lothaire depossederent, voire constituerent prisonnier Anastase Antipape, & restablirent Benoist, comme observe Sigebert. Ie dis de plus, que Marianus se mesprend avec Regino, quand il estime que l'Italie & le titre imperial, ont esté conferez à Louys fils aisné de Lothai-re à l'heure du partage, & en vertu d'iceluy seulement. Car par le recit d'Ado auteur contemporain & subjet de Lothaire, il conste que ce Prince envoya à Rome son fils Louys, qu'il avoit fait Roy d'Italie, afin {1}qu'il receuft le nom d'Empereur par l'intervention de Dreux Evesque de Metz son oncle; que Sergius des lors Pape, l'a couronné & qu'il fut salué Empereur & Auguste, tout le peuple faisant des acclamations; & Anastase en la vie de Sergius, nous advertit que le voyage de Louys & de Dreux son grand oncle se fit en Fevrier 844; & par consequent que Louys avoit esté honoré du titre Royal par son Pere, des le commencement de l'année, ou auparavant: Mesme (corrigeant tresiustement Ado) il asseure que Sergius oignit Louys , le couronna & l'establit pour Roy sur les Lombards ; mais refusa de luy prester serment , qui estoit en effect luy denier le nom & la puissance Imperiale , dont il fut investi par Leon IV l'an 849, comme ainsi soit que le titre du Concile de Pavie porte , {2} qu'il a esté assemblé l'an 851 de l'incarnation,& le 35 de Lothaire, & Louys trespieux Augustes ; que le Concile assemblé à Rome le 8 Decembre 853 compte lors la 5 année de l'Empire de Louys, & que le second Concile de Pavie se trouve assemblé l'an du Seigneur 854, le 6 de l'Empereur Louys en l'indiction 2. De façon qu'il est absolument impossible que Marianus contredit par tant de documens authentiques ne se soit point trompé, & de là mesme doit estre corrigée la Chronique de S. Bertin, qui faisant un mescompte d'un an cotte sur l'année 850, que Lothaire envoya son fils Louys à Rome, qui fut receu honorablement par le Pape Leon, & oint Empereur.
units.tr: He adds, after Regino, under the year 855, which was the fifteenth and last year of the Emperor Lothair: having summoned the chief men of the kingdom, he divided the empire among his sons, gave Italy to Louis and had him called Emperor by his own name. To Lothair he granted the kingdom that bears his name. To Charles, the youngest of them, he committed Provence. Having made this disposition, he left the world, came to the monastery of Prüm, and in the same year died on 29 September, after he had taken the habit of the holy fellowship of monks. I agree about the division Lothair made among his children, about his retirement to Prüm, and about his death, which followed immediately afterwards. But I maintain that, before Lothair died, Benedict III had been raised by the Romans to the place of Leo IV, since the decree of his election had been sent to Lothair, as Anastasius and Liutprand specifically note; that the messengers of Hincmar, who were making their way to Rome with the ambassadors of the same Lothair, found Benedict sitting in Leo's place when they arrived; and that the ambassadors of Lothair deposed, indeed took prisoner, the antipope Anastasius, and restored Benedict, as Sigebert observes. I say further that Marianus is mistaken with Regino when he thinks that Italy and the imperial title were conferred on Louis, the eldest son of Lothair, at the time of the division and by virtue of it alone. For from the account of Ado, a contemporary author and a subject of Lothair, it is established that this prince sent to Rome his son Louis, whom he had made king of Italy, so that he might receive the name of Emperor through the mediation of Drogo, Bishop of Metz, his uncle; that Sergius, who was then pope, crowned him, and that he was hailed as Emperor and Augustus, with all the people acclaiming. Anastasius, in the life of Sergius, also tells us that the journey of Louis and of Drogo, his great-uncle, took place in February 844; and consequently Louis had been honoured with the royal title by his father at the beginning of that year or earlier. Moreover (correcting Ado very justly) he assures us that Sergius anointed Louis, crowned him, and established him as king over the Lombards, but refused to take an oath of allegiance to him, which in effect was to deny him the name and power of Emperor, with which he was invested by Leo IV in the year 849. Since the title of the Council of Pavia reads {2} that it was assembled in the year 851 of the incarnation, and in the thirty-fifth year of Lothair, and of Louis, most pious Augustuses; since the council assembled at Rome on 8 December 853 then counts the fifth year of the empire of Louis; and since the second Council of Pavia is found to have been assembled in the year of the Lord 854, in the sixth year of the Emperor Louis, in the second indiction, it is absolutely impossible that Marianus, contradicted by so many authentic documents, should not have been mistaken. And from this same point the Chronicle of St Bertin must also be corrected, which, making a miscount of one year too many for the year 850, says that Lothair sent his son Louis to Rome, who was honourably received by Pope Leo, and was anointed emperor.

units.la: Sur l'an 857, qui estoit le 3 du jeune Lothaire, Marianus fait cette remarque, Benoist 103 Pape apres Pierre a esté assis deux ans, six mois, & six jours; & j'ay desja demonstré que tresmal à propos il recule de 15 mois & plus, ce Prelat qui avoit esté establi solennellement le Dimanche 29 Septembre 855. Posons toutesfois qu'il faille commencer son establissement du 1 Ianvier 857: s'il a (comme Marianus presuppose) tenu le siege 2 ans, 6 mois, & 6 jours, sa mort sera necessairement arrivée le 6 Iuin 859. A quel propos donc releguer le Pape Nicolas I son successeur à l'an 860? Marianus pensoit il qu'il y eust eu du crime à ne pas feindre des longs interregnes apres la mort de chaque Pape ? Mais la verité est,qu'apres le trefpas deBenoist arrivé le Vendredy 8 Auril 858 , le fiege n'a prefque point vaqué,Nicolas ayant(comme remarque Anastase) esté sacré le Dimanche 24 du mesme mois ; & Marianus nous en donne , quand il insinue couvertement une vacation de 5 mois & 24 jours au moins.
units.tr: Under the year 857, which was the third year of the younger Lothair, Marianus makes this remark: Benedict, the 103rd pope after Peter, sat for two years, six months and six days. I have already shown that he very wrongly pushes back by fifteen months and more this prelate, who had been solemnly established on Sunday, 29 September 855. Let us nevertheless suppose that his establishment must be dated from 1 January 857. If he held the see for 2 years, 6 months and 6 days (as Marianus presupposes), his death must necessarily have occurred on 6 June 859. Why then relegate his successor, Pope Nicholas I, to the year 860? Did Marianus think there was some crime in not feigning long interregnums after the death of each pope? But the truth is that after the death of Benedict, which occurred on Friday, 8 April 858, the see was hardly vacant at all, Nicholas having (as Anastasius remarks) been consecrated on Sunday, 24 of the same month; and Marianus gives us this when he covertly suggests a vacancy of at least five months and twenty-four days.

units.la: Sur l'année 860 , qui estoit la 5 du jeune Lothaire il dit, Nicolas 104 apres Pierre a esté assis 8 ans, & 6 jours. En quoy il se trompe lourdement , avec la Compilation Chronologique , qui commence le Papat de Nicolas à l'an 860 , le termine à l'an 870; & luy assigne la durée de 10 ans & 1 mois, & Godefroy de Viterbe qui ( pour faire place à Paul & Estienne Papes imaginaires , qu'il introduit entre Benoist & Nicolas) recule le Pontificat de ce dernier de 15 ans. Nicolas a donc tenu le fiege depuis le Dimanche 24 Auril 858, jufques au 13 Novembre 867 , neuf ans , six mois, & 20 jours durant. Ce qui est attesté par Anastase le Bibliothecaire, Luitprand, les Annales de S. Bertin & de Fulde , Herman , Honoré d'Austun , Florent de Worcester,l'Abbé d'Vrsperg, Matthieu de Westmonstier &c. Mais posons (pour gratifier Marianus ) qu'il n'a esté installé au siege que l'an 860, & n'y est demeuré que 8 ans & 9 jours ; à ce compte il fera necessairement decedé dans l'an 868, & Marianus datant sa mort de l'an 869 nous aura entretenu de ses resveries. Car quand (pour allonger de pres d'un an l'interregne qu'il a feint entre Benoist & Nicolas) il n'auroit pas trouvé bon de commencer le Papat du dernier avant la fin de Decemb. en 860,encor auroit il eu de la peine à conduire sa vie jusques à l'entrée de l'an 869.
units.tr: Under the year 860, which was the fifth year of the younger Lothair, he says: Nicholas, the 104th after Peter, sat for 8 years and 6 days. In this he errs grossly, along with the Chronological Compilation, which begins the papacy of Nicholas in the year 860, ends it in the year 870, and assigns to it a duration of 10 years and 1 month; and with Godfrey of Viterbo, who (to make room for the imaginary popes Paul and Stephen, whom he introduces between Benedict and Nicholas) pushes back the pontificate of the latter by 15 years. Nicholas therefore held the see from Sunday, 24 April 858, until 13 November 867, nine years, six months and 20 days in all. This is attested by Anastasius the Librarian, Liutprand, the Annals of St Bertin and of Fulda, Hermann, Honorius of Autun, Florence of Worcester, the Abbot of Ursberg, Matthew of Westminster, etc. But let us suppose (to oblige Marianus) that he was installed in the see only in the year 860 and remained there only 8 years and 9 days; on that reckoning he must necessarily have died in the year 868, and Marianus, dating his death in the year 869, would have been telling us his dreams. For even if (in order to lengthen by nearly a year the interregnum he invented between Benedict and Nicholas) he had not thought fit to begin the papacy of the latter before the end of December 860, he would still have had difficulty in carrying his life on to the beginning of the year 869.

units.la: Or ce qui le confond entierement est que sur ladite année 869 , qui estoit la 14 de Lothaire , il escrit, S. Nicolas Pape est mort le 8 des Ides de Decembre , c'est à dire (comme nous comptons) le 6 du mesme mois. En quoy il n'y a pas un mot de verité. Car sans m'arrester à demander , de quel droit Marianus qualifie Saint celuy que Rome n'a point inseré dans son Martyrologe, apres avoir refusé ce titre à Leon IV qu'elle y a placé : Je remarque non seulement que Nicolas n'est decedé ni l'an 869, ni en Decemb. mais aussi qu'il ne l'a peu selon l'hypothese pretendue de Marianus. Veu que (s'il a tenu le siege 8 ans 9 jours à commencer de l'an 860) il est necessairement mort l'an 868 ; & si (ayant esté assis 8 ans & 9 jours precisement ) il est mort le 6 Decembre 869 , il faut (de toute necessité) que son establissement n'ayt commencé que le Vendredy 28 Novembre 861 , & par consequent que Marianus ayt eu la cervelle renversée , pour la barbouiller de tant de Chimeres ; & que ce seroit se faire un extreme tort de se fier à la conduite d'un guide si estrangement esgaré.
units.tr: What utterly confounds him, however, is that under that year 869, which was the fourteenth year of Lothair, he writes: St Nicholas the Pope died on the 8th of the Ides of December, that is (as we reckon) on 6 December of the same month. There is not one word of truth in this. For, without stopping to ask by what right Marianus calls Saint one whom Rome has not inserted in her Martyrology, after refusing that title to Leo IV, whom she has placed there, I observe not only that Nicholas did not die in the year 869, nor in December, but also that, on Marianus's own hypothesis, he could not have done so. For if he held the see for 8 years and 9 days counting from the year 860, he necessarily died in 868; and if (having sat for precisely 8 years and 9 days) he died on 6 December 869, then his establishment must have begun on Friday, 28 November 861, and consequently Marianus must have had his brain turned, to daub it with so many chimeras; and it would be an extreme wrong to trust the guidance of a guide so strangely led astray.

units.la: Or afin qu'il conste à tous de l'abus, & que la verité produite avec ses lumieres naturelles, donne directement dans la veuë des moins clairvoyans ; ayant presupposé que Anastase & Luitprand & la Chronique de S. Bertin marquent la mort de Nicolas au 13 Novembre 867, l'observe 1, que Guillaume le Bibliothecaire en la vie d'Adrian second (se proposant de faire voir qu'à chaque vacance de siege depuis l'an 850 les yeux de toute Rome avoient esté sur ce Prelat elevé de la main de Gregoire I V) escrit, que comme apres la mort du Pape Leon IV , ainsi apres le decez de Benoist III Pontife , on l'avoit contraint de subir la charge pontificale ; excluant formellement la pretendue Ieanne , & faisant suivre Leon , & Benoist , immediatement apres Sergius : & ( pour nous marquer de trois caracteres infaillibles le temps de l'election d'Adrian) adjoufte, que le jour de Dimanche (selon la coustume) il fut mené en l'Eglise de S. Pierre le 19 des Kalendes de Janvier, ou (comme nous comptons ordinairement) le 14 Decemb. Indiction premiere, l'an 19 de Louys Auguste. Car ni le 19 de Louys, ni le 14 Decembre de l'indiction premiere, ni le Dimanche escheant au 14 Decembre, ne conviennent qu'à l'an 867: le 868 ayant esté signalé par le 20 de Louys, par le commencement de l'indiction seconde, & par le Mardy 14 Decembre; & le 869 par le 21 de Louys, par le commencement de l'indiction 3, & par le Mercredy 14 Decemb. de façon que ceux qui font estat de suivre en cet endroit le calcul de Marianus, pour establir (à son imitation) le Papat de sa Jeanne en terre; bouleversent sans y penser le cours invariable du Ciel, & jettent dans un desreglement honteux l'ordre immuable des temps, la revolution des indictions,& les characteres des feries, qui dependent tellement de la providence de Dieu, qu'ils ne sont nullement à la merci des Romans, ni de ceux qui les protegent.
units.tr: Now, so that it is plain to everyone where the abuse lies, and so that the truth, with its natural light, shines directly into the eyes of even the least perceptive: I have assumed that Anastasius, Luitprand and the Chronicle of St Bertin place Nicholas's death on 13 November 867. I observe that William the Librarian, in his life of Adrian II (intending to show that at every vacancy of the see since 850 the eyes of all Rome had turned to this prelate, raised up by Gregory IV), writes that just as after the death of Pope Leo IV, so after the decease of Pope Benedict III they forced him to undertake the pontifical office. He thus formally excludes the supposed Joan and makes Leo and Benedict follow immediately after Sergius. And, to mark the time of Adrian's election by three infallible signs, he adds that on Sunday (according to custom) he was led to the church of St Peter on the 19th of the Kalends of January, which (as we ordinarily count) is 14 December, first indiction, the 19th year of Louis Augustus. For the 19th year of Louis, 14 December in the first indiction, and a Sunday falling on 14 December, all agree only with the year 867. The year 868 was marked by the 20th year of Louis, by the beginning of the second indiction, and by Tuesday 14 December; and 869 by the 21st year of Louis, by the beginning of the third indiction, and by Wednesday 14 December. So those who intend to follow Marianus's calculation here, in order to establish (in his imitation) the papacy of their Joan on earth, unknowingly disturb the unchanging course of heaven, and throw into shameful disorder the immutable order of times, the revolution of the indictions and the characters of the weekdays, which depend so entirely on the providence of God that they are in no way at the mercy of the Romans or of those who protect them.

units.la: Je prie les Lecteurs de peser cette remarque des Annales de S. Bertin, qui asseurent,que l'an 868 la 4 ferie apres le commencement du Carefme (par consequent le 10 Mars) Arfenius & fon fils Eleuthere enleverent la fille du Pape Adrian, qu'ils la menerent à Benevent, qu'Arfenius mourut peu apres, que le Pape ayant fait plainte de cet attentat, Eleuthere assassina la fille avec Stephanie sa mere femme du Pape, & qu'il fut en fin tué par les messagers de l'Empereur. Car de cette histoire resulte qu'Adrian II tenoit le siege des le commencement de l'an 868. Et les annales de Fulde cottent sur la mesme année, que le Roy Lothaire s'estant acheminé à Rome, tascha par grande affection de se conjoindre par mariage Waldrade, avec le consentement & faveur de Nicolas Pontife; mais le trouvant desja mort, il alla à Benevent vers son frere Louys, & le requit de favoriser cet accouplement pres d'Adrian qui a succedé à Nicolas au Pontificat. Car comme de là appert, que Lothaire arrivant à Rome depuis le 13 Novembre 867, avoit trouvé Adrian II assis en la place de Nicolas I; il s'en recueille necessairement que Nicolas estoit decedé devant l'an 869, voire devant l'an 868; puisque l'an 868 Lothaire avoit besoin de la faveur de son frere Louys pres du Pape Adrian II.
units.tr: I ask the readers to weigh this remark of the Annals of St Bertin, which assert that in the year 868, on the fourth feria after the beginning of Lent (that is, 10 March), Arsenius and his son Eleutherius carried off the daughter of Pope Adrian, and took her to Benevento; that Arsenius died soon after; that when the Pope complained of this outrage, Eleutherius murdered the daughter together with Stephanie, her mother, the Pope's wife; and that he was finally killed by the messengers of the Emperor. For this story shows that Adrian II held the see from the beginning of the year 868. The Annals of Fulda also record for the same year that King Lothair, having set out for Rome, strove with great eagerness to join himself in marriage to Waldrade, with the consent and favour of Pope Nicholas; but finding him already dead, he went to Benevento to his brother Louis, and asked him to favour this union with Adrian, who succeeded Nicholas in the pontificate. For it appears from this that Lothair, arriving at Rome after 13 November 867, found Adrian II seated in the place of Nicholas I. It follows necessarily that Nicholas had died before 869, indeed before 868, since in 868 Lothair needed the favour of his brother Louis with Pope Adrian II.

units.la: 3. Ie presse les certificats des Annales de S.Bertin, & de Metz, de Regino, Herman & Lambert de Schafnabourg, qui portent que le Lundy 8 Aoust 869 Lothaire retournant de Rome, où il avoit esté accueilly honorablement par le Pontife Adrian, mourut à Plaisance où sa maladie l'avoit arresté. car si le Pape Nicolas est decedé seulement le 6 Decembre 869, selon l'imagination de Marianus, comment s'est il peu faire qu'Adrian successeur de Nicolas l'ait honorablement receu, & abfous 4 mois auparavant ?
units.tr: Thirdly, I press the testimony of the Annals of St Bertin and of Metz, and of Regino, Hermann and Lambert of Schaffhausen, who report that on Monday 8 August 869 Lothair, returning from Rome, where he had been honourably received by the Pontiff Adrian, died at Piacenza, where his illness had detained him. For if Pope Nicholas died only on 6 December 869, as Marianus imagines, how could Adrian, Nicholas's successor, have honourably received him and absolved him four months earlier?

units.la: 4. Je produis en tesmoignage contre Marianus, les Epistres du Pape Adrian; Par exemple, celle qu'il a escrite le 2 Fevrier 868 au Concile de Troyes; celles qu'il a envoyées le 12 du mesme mois au Roy Louys, & aux Evesques de Germanie; & le 27 à Actard Evesque de Nantes; le 6 Mars à Hincmar & Erard Archevefques de Rheims & de Tours; le 7 du mesme mois au Roy Charles le Chauve; le 1 Aoust à Basile Empereur d'Orient, & à Ignace Patriarche de Constantinople; & le 10 Juin 869 au mesme Ignace: item le Concile assemblé à Rome peu auparavant, & inseré es actes du Concile assemblé à Constantinople contre Photius; & finalement le Concile de Constantinople, dont les actes portent qu'il a esté assemblé l'an 3 du Consulat des amis de Christ & trespieux Empereurs Basile & Constantin perpetuels Auguftes, indiction 3 le 5 Octob. un Mercredy, dans le temple de Sophie la S. & de grand nom, où assistoyent {1}Donat & Estienne Evesques tres-aimez de Dieu, & Marin venerable Diacre, tenans le lieu d'Adrian le tres-saint & tresheureux Archevesque de la vieille Rome. Car si Adrian es années 868 & 869 a (en qualité de Pape) escrit des lettres, assemblé des Conciles, & envoyé des Legats : quel lieu peut plus rester à la resverie de Marianus, tirant (en despit de tous les monumens que l'antiquité nous a laissez) le pontificat de Nicolas I, jusques au 6 Decembre 869, qui achevoit la seconde année de celuy d'Adrian son successeur ? Il eust esté fort à desirer, que ces choses trescertaines & indubitables, eussent esté mises en confideration par tous ceux qui se laissans (avec trop de bonne foy) preoccuper à l'autorité de Marianus, ont pris de sa main sur bon compte, tout ce qu'il a mis en avant touchant les années de Leon IV, Benoist III, & Nicolas I, qu'il a taillées à sa mode pour faire reserve à sa Jeanne, qui n'eut jamais d'autre pere que son imagination, d'une place honorable & commode. Mais le credit que la reputation de son sçavoir (non commun pour le temps ) luy avoit acquis en l'opinion des hommes , ayant tellement prevalu par dessus la voix de la verité , qu'elle a esté comme contrainte de souffrir du rebut durant pres de cinq siecles ; il ne faut pas que le nostre illustré de beaucoup plus de connoissances demeure tache du mesme opprobre, & trouve raisonnable de flatter un vieil erreur à cause qu'il a long temps duré : ni que Rome aujourd'huy (à dessein de descharger & Marianus,& Martinus Polonus de blasme) s'amuse à accuser les copistes de leurs Chroniques , & (se vantant d'en avoir des exemplaires manuscrits qui ne parlent point de la Papesse ) soustienne que les autres sur lesquels les editions ont esté faites , ont esté alterez depuis. Car comme chacun scait que les manuscripts sont tels qu'il plait à ceux qui les transcrivent , je suis certain qu'il est impossible que l'on en produise ( de quelque part que ce puisse estre ) qui nous donne la Chronique de Marianus exempte des fautes remarquées cy dessus , & de la veüe desquelles resulte necessairement , que s'il se trouve ( ou que ce soit) quelque exemplaire de cet auteur qui ne face point mention de sa Papesse il est nouveau & corrompu : toute l'œconomie de fon ouvrage, requerant que fon lieu propre luy foit gardé mesmes au prejudice des Papes antecedens & subsequens. & le mesme se peut dire à l'egard de Martinus Polonus, de qui l'esprit a esté capable de telles productions, & l'escrit est parsemé de quantité de sottises qui ne doivent rien à la fable de Marianus, que cet homme a parée tant qu'il a peu.
units.tr: Fourthly, I produce against Marianus the Epistles of Pope Adrian. For example, the one he wrote on 2 February 868 to the Council of Troyes; those he sent on the 12th of the same month to King Louis and to the bishops of Germany; and on the 27th to Actard, Bishop of Nantes; on 6 March to Hincmar and Erard, archbishops of Reims and Tours; on the 7th of the same month to King Charles the Bald; on 1 August to Basil, Emperor of the East, and to Ignatius, Patriarch of Constantinople; and on 10 June 869 to the same Ignatius. Likewise there is the Council assembled at Rome shortly before, inserted in the acts of the Council assembled at Constantinople against Photius; and finally the Council of Constantinople, whose acts state that it was assembled in the 3rd year of the consulship of Basil and Constantine, friends of Christ and pious perpetual Augusti, in the third indiction, on 5 October, a Wednesday, in the temple of Holy Wisdom, great and renowned, where there were present {1}Donatus and Stephen, bishops most beloved of God, and Marinus, venerable deacon, holding the place of Adrian, the most holy and most blessed archbishop of old Rome. For if Adrian, in the years 868 and 869, as Pope wrote letters, convened councils and sent legates, what room can remain for Marianus's dreaming, which, in defiance of all the monuments that antiquity has left us, stretches the pontificate of Nicholas I to 6 December 869, the day that completed the second year of that of his successor Adrian? It would have been greatly to be wished that these most certain and indubitable things had been taken into consideration by all those who, allowing themselves (with too much good faith) to be preoccupied by the authority of Marianus, have accepted on trust from his hand everything he put forward concerning the years of Leo IV, Benedict III and Nicholas I, which he cut to his own fashion to make room for his Joan, who never had any father but his imagination, in an honourable and convenient place. But the credit which the reputation of his learning (uncommon for the time) had won him in the opinion of men has so far prevailed over the voice of truth that it has been compelled, as it were, to suffer rejection for nearly five centuries. Our own age, illuminated by far more knowledge, ought not to remain stained by the same disgrace, nor to think it reasonable to flatter an old error merely because it has lasted a long time. Nor should Rome today, in order to clear Marianus and Martin of Troppau of blame, amuse itself by accusing the copyists of their chronicles, and, boasting of having manuscript copies that say nothing of the Popess, maintain that the others on which the printed editions were based have been altered since. For as everyone knows, manuscripts are such as those who copy them please, and I am certain it is impossible to produce, from any quarter whatever, a copy of Marianus's Chronicle free of the faults noted above. From the sight of these faults it necessarily follows that if some copy of this author is found (wherever it may be) that makes no mention of his Popess, it is recent and corrupted. The whole economy of his work requires that her proper place be kept for her, even to the prejudice of the preceding and following Popes. The same may be said of Martin of Troppau, whose mind was capable of such productions, and whose writing is strewn with a host of foolish things that owe nothing to Marianus's fable, which this man has embellished as far as he could.

units.la: Quant à Sigebert, voicy ce que nous avons de luy sur l'an 844 du Seigneur, auquel il adapte le 4 de l'Empereur Lothaire, & le 14 de Theophile Empereur d'Orient decedé des l'an 841. Sergius preside le centieme sur l'Eglise Romaine. Item sur l'an 847, septieme de Lothaire & 2 de Michel fils de Theophile avec Theodora sa mere : Leon cinquieme preside le cent unieme sur l'Eglise Romaine. & à cela je ne trouve rien à reprendre, sinon que mal à propos il appelle cinquieme celuy qui estoit quatrieme en effect. Mais sur l'an 854, quatorzieme de Lothaire & neufvieme de Michel Porphyrogenete avec Theodora, nous faisons une pire rencontre es paroles suivantes : Jean l'Anglois ; le bruit est que ce Jean a esté femme, & connüe d'un seul de ses familiers, qui l'embrassa, & qu'estant grosse, elle a enfanté estant Pape. C'est pourquoy quelques uns ne la comptent pas entre les Pontifes : & pourtant elle ne fait point de nombre par son nom. Hincmar Archevesque de Rheims qui a escrit la vie de S. Remy est en reputation entre les François. Benoist cent deuxieme preside sur l'Eglise Romaine. Cetuy-cy ayant esté deposé par la conspiration des malins, Anastase envahit la Prelature ; mais Anastase ayant esté mis bas par les legats de l'Empereur Lothaire, & coigné en prison, Benoist est remis honorablement en sa place. Je dis donc que (demeurant d'accord tant de ce qui est dit de la reputation d'Hincmar, qui le 1 Janu. 854 avoit desja passé sept mois & demi de la 9 année de son Archiepiscopat ; que de l'effort d'Anastase contre Benoist,& de l'issue de son schisme) Sigebert a manqué lors qu'il en a fait le rapport sous l'an 854: veu 1 que (selon qu'il a esté demonstré cy dessus) Leon IV a vescu jusqu'au 17 Juillet 855, & Benoist a esté restabli le Dimanche 29 Septembre suivant : & d'ailleurs, que la clause qui traitte de Jean l'Anglois, ne peut subsister, ni avec la suitte qui parle de Benoist, ni avec l'opinion de Marianus : Car (directement contre le sentiment de Marianus) elle change la Papesse de place, la produisant un an plus tard, & la fait paroistre en mesme temps que Benoist, quoy qu'il ne se trouve aucun Auteur, qui die que Benoist (qui a eu assez à faire à colletter Anastase) ayt esté son concurrent. Ioint que s'il falloit interpreter Sigebert en cette forte, que Ieanne soit perie l'an 854 avant l'establissement de Benoist & le schisme d'Anastase, & qu'elle ayt tenu le siege 2 ans, 5 mois, & 4 jours, comme veut Marianus; bien loin d'accorder 8 années à Leon IV, comme Marianus, ou 8 ans, 3 mois & quelques jours, comme les autres, il faudroit necessairement retrancher de son pontificat 3 années & plus, & luy en laisser moins de six pour donner temps à Ieanne, de monter sur le siege, des l'an 852, un an plustost que ne veut Marianus. C'est pourquoy, en ces paroles qui la concernent (de qui qu'elles soient) il n'y a ny raison, ny ombre de raison.
units.tr: As for Sigebert, here is what we have from him under the year 847 of the Lord, to which he assigns the fourth year of the Emperor Lothair and the fourteenth of Theophilus, Emperor of the East, who died in 841: Sergius presides as the hundredth over the Roman Church. Again, under the year 847, the seventh of Lothair and the second of Michael, son of Theophilus, together with his mother Theodora: Leo the fifth presides as the hundred and first over the Roman Church. I find nothing to object to here, except that he wrongly calls fifth the man who was in fact the fourth. But under the year 854, the fourteenth of Lothair and the ninth of Michael Porphyrogenitus with Theodora, we meet with a worse error in the following words: John the Englishman. The report is that this John was a woman, and was known by one only of her intimates, who embraced her; and that, being pregnant, she gave birth while she was Pope. For this reason some do not count her among the pontiffs; and yet she does not make up a number by her name. Hincmar, Archbishop of Reims, who wrote the life of Saint Remigius, is held in high esteem among the French. Benedict the hundred and second presides over the Roman Church. He, having been deposed by the conspiracy of the wicked, Anastasius seized the prelacy; but Anastasius, having been cast down by the legates of the Emperor Lothair and thrown into prison, Benedict was honourably restored to his place. I say, therefore, that (while agreeing both with what is said of Hincmar's reputation, who by 1 January 854 had already passed seven and a half months of the ninth year of his archiepiscopate, and with the attempt of Anastasius against Benedict and the outcome of his schism) Sigebert erred when he made this report under the year 854. For, first, (as has been demonstrated above) Leo IV lived until 17 July 855, and Benedict was restored on Sunday, 29 September following. And further, the clause which deals with John the Englishman cannot stand, either with the sequel that speaks of Benedict, or with the opinion of Marianus. For (directly contrary to the view of Marianus) it moves the Papess to another place, placing her a year later, and makes her appear at the same time as Benedict, although there is no author who says that Benedict (who had enough to do in getting rid of Anastasius) had a rival. Moreover, if Sigebert had to be interpreted in this way, that Joan perished in 854 before the establishment of Benedict and the schism of Anastasius, and that she held the see 2 years, 5 months and 4 days, as Marianus wishes, then, far from granting 8 years to Leo IV, as Marianus does, or 8 years, 3 months and some days, as the others do, it would be necessary to cut 3 years or more from his pontificate, and leave him fewer than six, to allow time for Joan to mount the see as early as 852, a year sooner than Marianus claims. Therefore, in these words concerning her (whoever wrote them) there is neither reason nor shadow of reason.

units.la: Sigebert adjoufte sur l'an 855, quinzieme de Lothaire, & dixieme de Michel avec Theodora : Lothaire Empereur ayant partagé le royaume entre ses fils, renonce au siecle, & ayant pris l'habit monastique au monastere de Prom, non long temps apres s'endormit au Seigneur. En effet sa mort arriva, selon Regino, le propre jour, & selon les Annales de S. Bertin, la veille de l'establissement solennel de Benoist III, le Dimanche 29 Septembre 855. & cette remarque (qui sappe le fondement de la supposition de Marianus) oblige d'autant plus Sigebert à s'en départir, qu'il a expressement reconnu que les legats de Lothaire avoient restabli Benoist, & debutté Anastase son competiteur.
units.tr: Sigebert adds, under the year 855, the fifteenth of Lothair and the tenth of Michael with Theodora: The Emperor Lothair, having divided the kingdom among his sons, renounced the world, and, having taken the monastic habit at the monastery of Prüm, not long afterwards fell asleep in the Lord. Indeed, according to Regino, his death occurred on the very same day, and according to the Annals of Saint Bertin, on the day before the solemn establishment of Benedict III, Sunday, 29 September 855. And this observation (which undermines the foundation of Marianus's supposition) obliges Sigebert all the more to depart from it, since he has expressly acknowledged that the legates of Lothair restored Benedict and deposed Anastasius, his rival.

units.la: Vient en suitte l'année 857, seconde de l'Empereur Louys II, & à son compte premiere deMichel seul; sur laquelle il fait cette remarque : Nicolas (de qui l'Empereur Louys autoriza l'ordination par sa presence) preside le cent troisieme sur l'Eglise Romaine ; r'apportant à l'an 857 ce qui appartenoit au Dimanche 24 Auril 858: car ayant avancé l'ordination de Benoist III un an plus qu'il ne devoit, il a esté contraint de tirer aussi à proportion celle de Nicolas, & la placer hors de son propre lieu. Neantmoins r'entrant dans l'ordre sur l'an 868, treizieme de Louys, & selon son compte 12 de Michel, il fait mention d'Adrian disant : Adrian preside le cent quatrième sur l'Eglise Romaine ; & cela tres à propos: car Adrian ayant esté inthronizé le Dimanche 14 Decembre 867, estoit encore dans le 19 jour de son premier mois, quand l'an 868 commença. mais il s'abuse en remettant la mort de Michel à l'an 869, veu qu'il avoit efté tué par Bafile le Macedonien le 23 Septembre 867, au commencement de la premiere indiction: de mesme qu'il s'eft mefpris en difpofant les années du mefme Michel, qui avoit fuccedé à Theophile au commencement de l'an 841, & depoffedé Theodora fa mere l'an 855, & non es années 846, & 856, comme il a mal prefuppofé. Quoy que fon mefcompte ne trouble pas fort la fucceffion des Papes, & ne foit en rien comparable à celuy de Marianus, je n'ay pas eftimé jufte de le diffimuler, ni de laiffer prendre pour bien dit par luy,ce qui n'eftoit pas conforme à la verité. Et pource qu'aujourd'huy Rome tient qu'il n'a point du tout parlé de la Papeffe, que l'original de fa Chronique eft encor en fon entier à Gemblours pour en faire foy, & que d'autres ont amplifié depuis fon difcours là où ils l'ont creu (felon le prejugé dont ils eftoient imbus) defectueux & peu complet. Voyant que Vincent de Beauvais, Alberic, & Guillaume de Nangis (qui ont d'année en année inferé fes paroles dans leurs recueils, & particulierement à l'efgard de ce qu'il a efcrit fur l'année 854 touchant Benoift III, & Anaftafe fon Antipape; & fur l'année 857 touchant Nicolas premier) ne copient point la clausé concernant la Papesse ; que ses hypotheses confirment d'une part l'election de Benoist pendant le vivant de Lothaire, & de l'autre combattent de front contre l'establissement de la pretendue Ieanne ; & qu'il est impossible de luy attribuer les paroles qui representent sa miserable fin, sans le jetter dans l'un de ces deux inconveniens, qu'il luy ait fait tenir le siege en mesme temps avec Benoist ; ou qu'il luy ait taillé son partage des roignures du Pontificat de Leon, qui se trouveroit diminué de pres de moitié s'il avoit cessé des l'an 852 : je ne puis pas penser qu'il faille beaucoup resister à cette opinion, ni s'opiniastrer à la contredire, sans avoir en main des preuves bien expresses & certaines du contraire.
units.tr: Next comes the year 857, the second of the Emperor Louis II, and by his reckoning the first of Michael alone; on which he makes this remark: Nicholas (whose ordination the Emperor Louis authorised by his presence) presides as the hundred and third over the Roman Church; he carries back to the year 857 what belonged to Sunday, 24 April 858, for, having brought forward the ordination of Benedict III by one year more than he should, he was compelled to draw that of Nicholas forward proportionately too, and place it outside its proper place. Nevertheless, returning to the sequence under the year 868, the thirteenth of Louis and, by his reckoning, the twelfth of Michael, he mentions Adrian, saying: Adrian presides as the hundred and fourth over the Roman Church; and this quite properly, for Adrian, having been enthroned on Sunday, 14 December 867, was still on the nineteenth day of his first month when the year 868 began. But he is mistaken in putting the death of Michael in the year 869, since he had been killed by Basil the Macedonian on 23 September 867, at the beginning of the first indiction; just as he went wrong in arranging the years of the same Michael, who had succeeded Theophilus at the beginning of the year 841 and deposed his mother Theodora in the year 855, and not in the years 846 and 856, as he wrongly supposed. Although his miscalculation does not greatly disturb the succession of the Popes, and is in no way comparable to that of Marianus, I have not thought it right to conceal it, nor to allow what was not in accordance with the truth to be taken as well said by him. And since Rome today maintains that he never spoke at all of the Papess, that the original of his Chronicle is still intact at Gembloux to bear witness to this, and that others have since expanded his account where they believed (according to the prejudice with which they were imbued) it to be defective and incomplete; seeing that Vincent of Beauvais, Alberic and William of Nangis (who from year to year inserted his words into their compilations, and particularly with regard to what he wrote under the year 854 concerning Benedict III and Anastasius his antipope, and under the year 857 concerning Nicholas I) do not copy the clause concerning the Papess; that his hypotheses, on the one hand, confirm the election of Benedict during the lifetime of Lothair, and on the other directly oppose the establishment of the so-called Joan; and that it is impossible to attribute to him the words which describe her wretched end without throwing him into one of these two difficulties, either that he made her hold the see at the same time as Benedict, or that he assigned her a share of the remnants of Leo's pontificate, which would have been reduced by nearly half had she ceased in 852: I cannot think that one should resist this opinion very hard, or obstinately contradict it, without having at hand very express and certain proofs to the contrary.

units.la: Ainsi ( selon que je puis appercevoir) Marianus est la premiere & seule source d'où tous les ruisseaux des Escrivains posterieurs sont derivez, & je ne croy pas (apres en avoir descouvert à nud le vice inexcusable) qu'il soit aucun besoin de passer plus avant en l'examen de ceux qui n'ont fait que copier les uns des autres, sans sçavoir si le premier avoit esté bien fondé. Quand les tesmoins se leveroient à centaines, voire à milliers pour donner des depositions digerées de la forte , il n'y auroit ame bien faite qui daignast avoir efgard , soit à leur nombre , qui ne devroit jamais faire de contrepoids contre la verité & la raison ; soit à leur discours , qui n'auroit esté en effet que le simple Echo des premieres resveries , qui eussent esté tres-aisées à convaincre d'impertinence & de faux , si ceux qui l'ont entrepris eussent plus eu le cœur à estudier l'histoire du 9 siecle , qu'à exercer cette eloquence mefdisante que S. Hierome eust en son temps appellée caninam facundiam, & que toutes gens d'honneur trouveront (plus qu'il ne se peut dire ) honteuse en des personnes qui veulent faire profession d'erudition, de gravité, & de sincerité.
units.tr: Thus (so far as I can see) Marianus is the first and only source from which all the streams of later writers flow. Having laid bare his inexcusable fault, I do not think it necessary to go further in examining those who merely copied one another without knowing whether the first account was well founded. Even if witnesses rose by hundreds, indeed by thousands, to give depositions drawn up in this manner, no sensible person would deign to have regard to them: not to their number, which should never count against truth and reason, nor to their argument, which would in fact be nothing but the simple echo of the first fancies. These could very easily have been refuted as absurd and false, had those who undertook it cared more to study the history of the ninth century than to practise that slanderous eloquence which St Jerome in his time called canine eloquence, and which all honourable people will find (more than can be said) shameful in persons who wish to profess learning, gravity and sincerity.

units.la: Car à quel propos constituer les Protestans , plus que les autres , responsables du fait de ceux qui les ont precedez de deux, voire de trois cens ans , & tirer leur nomen envie , & le barbouiller d'injures de cabaret , pource qu'ils ont admis de bonne foy , ce que les Papes , & la foule de leurs communicateurs avoient tellement autorizé par leur consentement, quil ne se trouvoit presque aucun contredisant ? A quoy servoit de se jetter à corps perdu (comme a fait celuy qui a emprunté le nom du S^r. de Remond ) sur des controverses hors de sujet, sinon à faire (s'il avoit esté possible) paroistre homme en Theologie, un picrocole qui se hasardoit à faire l'enfant en Histoire ? Et pourquoy arrester sa dispute à soustenir par de longs discours farcis d'injures ; la negative de certaines circonstances, qui (considerées absolument) n'ont rien du tout d'éloigné soit de la vray semblance, soit de la possibilité, sans penser si le sujet où toutes ces circonstances avoient esté bien ou mal attachées, estoit ou n'estoit pas destitué de fondement ? Qui empesche par exemple qu'une femme native (comme on suppose) de Mayence, n'ayt peu porter le surnom d'Anglois ; qu'ayant eu à couvrir une fourbe pourpensée, elle n'ayt peu se faire appeller de divers noms, tantost Gisleberte, & tantost Agnes, & de plus cacher sonsexe[?] ? Eugenie, Marine, & Euphrosyne n'ont elles pas (si on en croid les legendes) passé pour hommes ? La premiere n'a telle pas esté accusée d'avoir voulu forcer Melanthia ? & la seconde d'avoir violé de fait la fille d'un hostelier : ce qui ne fut reconnu qu'apres sa mort ? le recit du legendaire ne portet'il pas que la derniere ne se descouvrit qu'à son pere, à l'heure mesme qu'elle alloit expirer ? Ne dit on pas encore choses semblables, de Thecla compagne de S. Paul en habit desguisé, de Natalia femme du Martyr Adrian, de Theodora, de Pelagia, & d'autres ? & d'ailleurs qui eust osté le moyen à la pretendue Ieanne de se faire prendre pour homme en un temps auquel tous les Clercs estoient ras? Combien mesme void on d'hommes qui semblent ou effeminez, ou chastrez, & de femmes à l'oppofite qui font hommasses, & portent (quoy qu'en moindre quantité) du poil au menton ?
units.tr: For to what purpose make the Protestants, more than others, answerable for the deeds of those who went before them by two or even three hundred years, and drag their name through the mud and besmirch them with tavern insults, because they accepted in good faith what the Popes and the crowd of their adherents had so authorised by their consent that hardly anyone was found to contradict it? What was the point of throwing oneself headlong (as he did who borrowed the name of the Sieur de Remond) into controversies beside the point, except to make himself appear (if it were possible) a theologian, a Picrochole who ventured to play the child in history? And why rest one's dispute on maintaining, through long discourses stuffed with insults, the denial of certain circumstances which, considered in themselves, are in no way remote either from verisimilitude or from possibility, without considering whether the subject to which these circumstances were attached, rightly or wrongly, was or was not without foundation? What prevents, for example, a woman who was native (as is supposed) of Mainz from having borne the surname of Englishman; or, having a deceit to cover, from having been called by various names, now Gisleberta and now Agnes, and moreover from having hidden her sex? Were not Eugenia, Marina and Euphrosyne (if one believes the legends) taken for men? Was not the first accused of having wished to force Melanthia? And the second of having violated the innkeeper's daughter in fact, which was recognised only after her death? Does not the legendary account say that the last revealed herself only to her father, at the very hour she was about to expire? Are not similar things also told of Thecla, the companion of St Paul, in disguised dress; of Natalia, wife of the martyr Adrian; of Theodora, of Pelagia, and of others? And moreover, what would have prevented the so-called Joan from passing for a man at a time when all the clerks were shaven? Indeed, how many men are there who seem either effeminate or castrated, and women on the contrary who are mannish and have (though in smaller number) hair on the chin?

units.la: 2. On ne doit pas nier non plus qu'elle n'ayt peu courir diverses provinces & regions en cet habit desguisé : car combien de saincstes femmes ont elles esté par le seul desir de voir, tirées de l'Europe en l'Asie ? Cela n'est il pas arrivé à Melania, Paula, Eudocia, &c. Si des Dames de qualité si eminente ont peu se surmonter elles mesmes par une si forte resolution, combien a t'il esté aisé à quantité d'autres de moindre condition ; de la prendre, & avoler d'Occident dans les monasteres que les premieres avoient fondez sur le mont d'Olivet & en Bethlehem ? Et si l'on s'arreste au changement d'habits, n'asseure t'on pas que Thecla travestie fit le voyage de Lycaonie en Syrie, & de Syrie en Lycie, & Pelagia celuy d'Antioche de Syrie à Ierusalem? Et ce que l'on ose soustenir s'estre fait il y a 1200, voire 1590[?] ans, par quelle reigle estimera t'on qu'il soit devenu impossible apres l'an 800? 3. Qu'elle n'ayt peu s'arrester à Athenes pour l'estude; Car encor qu'Athenes & tout le reste de la Grece fussent (sous le 9 siecle) devenus fort grossiers, & barbares, & que les lettres ny eussent refleury que par le soin de Bardas, lors qu'ayant fait deposseder l'Imperatrice Theodora sa sœur, il se fut l'an 855 (c'est à dire au temps de la pretendue Ieanne, ou peu apres selon Marianus) saisi des resnes de l'Estat; neantmoins on avoit continué d'y parler Grec, & cela seul pouvoit suffire pour attirer un esprit curieux & desireux des lettres. 4. Qu'elle n'ayt peu se rendre capable d'enseigner la Theologie,& monter à un si haut faiste de reputation, que l'on l'ayt creuë digne du Papat: Car si Eugenie & Catherine ont (comme portent leurs legendes) esté tres-confommées en l'estude, jusques là que la premiere avoit imbu tous les secrets de la Philosophie, & la seconde refuté insurmontablement, à ce qu'on dit, 50 Orateurs, & si Marcella (selon le rapport de S. Hierome) a esté dans Rome mefme , fi celebre , & fi admirée, que quand il y avoit du debat pour quelque tefmoignage des Escritures, on la prenoit pour juge, voire fi elle a peu (quoy que reconnuë feulement pour femme) faire tefte à l'Origenifme qui fe g'iffoit tellement qu'il tiroit le confentement des Sacerdots,de quelques moines, & principalement des hommes du fiecle, & fe mocquoit de la fimplicité de l'Evefque Siricius ; à caufe de quoy auroit il (dans le 9 fiecle) efté impoffible à une femme prife pour homme,d'eftre confultée comme Docteur, & defirée comme Pape? 5. Quelle n'ayt peu accoucher en pleine proceffion. Car qu'y a t'il d'eftrange fi une femme de mauvaife vie, craignant la defcouverte de fa honte , & fe forçant plus que fa condition & le temps ne luy peuvent permettre , fait à toutes occafions de neceffité vertu , & s'expofe à la rifque des evenemens plus fafcheux ? 6. Que la rue où l'on tient qu'elle s'eft defchargée de fon fruit , n'ayt peu eftre en fi grande deteftation que depuis la proceffion s'en foit deftournée. Car {1} fi autresfois celle où la desnaturée Tullia fit traverser fon chariot fur le corps du Roy Servius fon pere , affaffiné à fa follicitation , a porté le nom de {2} mefchante ; pourquoy le honteux accident d'une fourbe facrilege n'auroit il point esmeu Rome à une semblable horreur ? 7. Que l'on n'ayt peu eriger une statue pour memoire d'un scandale si inouï. Car si Nismes en garde bien encore aujourd'huy une de Geryon dressée autresfois comme un monument consacré à l'eternité, en reconnoissance de la vengeance d'Hercule contre ce Tyran monstrueux, quelle raison aura t'on à produire, pour empescher que Rome n'ayt peu se porter à laisser des marques de son ressentiment & de son despit contre une sacrilege qui l'auroit si indignement trompée ? & si (comme raconte Socrate) Theophile d'Alexandrie apres avoir (par commandement du grand Theodose) demoli le temple de Serapis, & fracassé ou fondu les Idoles Payennes, jugeoit necessaire d'en exposer à la veuë du public une des plus ridicules, à sçavoir (si l'on en croid l'histoire Tripartite) celle d'un singe, pour faire une honte eternelle aux Payens, & leur oster tout moyen de nier qu'ils eussent jamais adoré pour Dieux des monstres : pourquoy Benoist III avec tout le Clergé, & peuple Romain, picqué d'une juste douleur pour l'affront qu'il venoit (comme on presuppose) de recevoir, n'auroit il peu se porter aisément à faire eriger, pour objet de perpetuelle horreur à la posterité, la statue de cette infame guenon, que l'on tient avoir eu l'effronterie de se faire venerer dans Rome comme une chose sainte?
units.tr: 2. Nor must it be denied that she may have been able to travel through various provinces and regions in this disguised dress: for how many holy women have been drawn from Europe into Asia by the mere desire to see? Has this not happened to Melania, Paula, Eudocia, and others? If ladies of such eminent rank could overcome themselves by so strong a resolution, how easy it must have been for many of lower condition to take her and to fly from the West into the monasteries which the former had founded on the Mount of Olives and at Bethlehem? And if one dwells on the change of clothing, is it not asserted that Thecla, disguised, made the journey from Lycaonia into Syria, and from Syria into Lycia, and Pelagia that from Antioch in Syria to Jerusalem? And what is maintained to have happened 1200, indeed 1590, years ago, by what rule will one judge it to have become impossible after the year 800? 3. That she may not have been able to stop at Athens for study: for although Athens and all the rest of Greece had (in the ninth century) become very coarse and barbarous, and letters had flourished again only through the care of Bardas, who, having deposed the Empress Theodora his sister, seized the reins of the state in the year 855 (that is, at the time of the so-called Joan, or shortly after, according to Marianus), nevertheless Greek had continued to be spoken there, and this alone could suffice to draw a curious mind eager for letters. 4. That she may not have been able to make herself capable of teaching theology, and to rise to such a height of reputation that she was thought worthy of the Papacy: for if Eugenia and Catherine were (as their legends report) very accomplished in study, so much so that the first had imbibed all the secrets of philosophy, and the second, it is said, refuted fifty orators beyond answer; and if Marcella (according to St Jerome's account) was in Rome itself so famous and so admired that when there was dispute over some testimony of the Scriptures, they took her as judge; indeed, if she was able (though recognised only as a woman) to withstand Origenism, which was spreading so that it drew the consent of priests, of some monks, and above all of men of the world, and mocked the simplicity of Bishop Siricius, then why, in the ninth century, would it have been impossible for a woman taken for a man to be consulted as a teacher and desired as Pope? 5. That she may not have been able to give birth in the middle of a procession. For what is strange about it, if a woman of bad life, fearing the discovery of her shame, and forcing herself beyond her condition and the time allow, makes a virtue of necessity on every occasion and exposes herself to the risk of more troublesome outcomes? 6. That the street where it is held she unloaded her fruit may not have been so detested that from then on the procession turned away from it. For {1} if formerly the street where the unnatural Tullia drove her chariot over the body of King Servius her father, murdered at her instigation, bore the name of {2} wicked, why should the shameful accident of a sacrilegious deceit not have stirred Rome to a similar horror? 7. That a statue could not have been erected in memory of so unheard-of a scandal. For if Nîmes still keeps even today one of Geryon, set up formerly as a monument consecrated to eternity, in acknowledgement of Hercules's vengeance upon that monstrous tyrant, what reason will be given to prevent Rome from having been able to leave marks of its resentment and its spite against a sacrilegious woman who had so shamefully deceived it? And if (as Socrates relates) Theophilus of Alexandria, after having (by command of the great Theodosius) demolished the temple of Serapis and smashed or melted down the pagan idols, judged it necessary to expose to public view one of the most ridiculous of them, namely (if one believes the Tripartite History) that of a monkey, to bring eternal shame upon the pagans and deprive them of all means of denying that they had ever worshipped monsters as gods: why would Benedict III, with all the clergy and the Roman people, stung by a just grief at the affront which he had (as is presupposed) just received, not have been able easily to resolve to have erected, as an object of perpetual horror for posterity, the statue of that infamous ape, which is held to have had the effrontery to be venerated at Rome as a holy thing?

units.la: 8. Que l'on n'ayt peu en fin arrefter, de faire seoir le Pape nouvellement eleu sur une felle percée, afin de discerner asseurement son sexe. Car encore que ce pretendu expedient soit goffe & vilain; puisque Rome mesme l'a creu recevable, & conforme à l'humeur du 9 siecle; à quel propos penserions nous seulement à nous formalizer contre le jugement qu'elle à fait de ceux qui l'ont conduitte pour lors?
units.tr: 8. That they could not finally be brought to seat the newly elected Pope on a perforated chair, so as to determine his sex with certainty. For although this supposed expedient is clumsy and vulgar, since Rome itself thought it acceptable and in keeping with the temper of the ninth century, why should we even think of taking offence at the judgment Rome passed on those who conducted her at that time?

units.la: Au lieu de se gendarmer (comme l'on a fait) contre des menus accessoires, la raison vouloit que ceux qui les ont impugnez s'attachassent directement au principal qui leur servoit de fondement, pour debattre s'il avoit esté, ou non. Car l'ayant posé comme arrivé de fait, ses suittes pouvoient se maintenir avec probabilité: au lieu qu'ayant impugné par l'histoire la possibilité de son existence, tout le reste fust tombé de soy mesme & sans autre dispute: veu que (selon le principe des Philosophes tres-evident en la lumiere de la nature) De ce qui n'est point, il n'y a point d'accidens. Mesme si l'on vouloit
units.tr: Instead of getting angry (as has been done) over minor accessories, reason required that those who attacked them should have gone straight to the principal matter on which they rested, to debate whether it had happened or not. For once it was posed as an actual fact, its consequences could stand with some probability. Whereas, once the possibility of its existence had been impugned by history, everything else would have fallen of itself and without further dispute, since (according to the principle of the Philosophers, very evident in the light of nature) there are no accidents of what does not exist. Even if one wished

units.la: Non entis non sunt accident-tia. faire quelque reflexion, sur les circonstances que nous avons representées, ce devoit estre seulement pour s'en prevaloir contre le prejugé de plusieurs, qui ont pensé sauver le Roman de Marianus contre le prejudice d'un silence de plus de 200 ans, en foustenant que les Auteurs qui ont vescu depuis l'an 855, jusqu'à l'an 1050; se font abstenus d'en parler, à cause de la honte qu'ils en avoient, & qu'ils ont mieux aimé alterer l'ordre de la succession des Papes par un silence affecté, que contribuer par l'expression d'une verité odieuse, à la conservation de l'execrable memoire de cette gouge, qui avoit (comme on pretend) deshonoré leur suitte, en s'y ingerant. Car laissant à part que les Auteurs du temps, expriment (selon qu'il a esté demonstré cy dessus) des veritez tres-contraires à cette supposition née depuis leur mort: ceux qui demeuroient à Rome comme Nicolas I, & Anastase, & Guillaume le Bibliothecaire, eussent eu le sens tout à fait troublé, s'ils eussent pensé pouvoir (par l'effort de leur silence & de leur honte) ensevelir une ordure que l'on suppose avoir tellement comblé Rome d'estonnement, d'indignation, & de scandale, qu'elle n'ayt peu se satisfaire qu'en eternizant l'effect de son juste desdain, & en proposant des marques perpetuelles à la posterité, par l'erection d'une statue representant la cause de son despit, par le destour de ses processions, & par l'introduction de couftumes inouiës auparavant, & peu honnestes.
units.tr: There are no accidents of what does not exist. to make some reflection on the circumstances we have set out, it ought only to have been to use them against the prejudice of many who have thought to save the Roman of Marianus from the prejudice of a silence of more than 200 years, by maintaining that the authors who lived from the year 855 to the year 1050 abstained from speaking of it because of the shame they felt, and preferred to alter the order of the succession of the Popes by a deliberate silence rather than contribute, by stating an odious truth, to the preservation of the execrable memory of that harlot, who had (as is claimed) dishonoured their line by intruding into it. For, leaving aside that the authors of the time express (as has been demonstrated above) truths very contrary to this supposition, born after their death: those who lived at Rome, such as Nicholas I, Anastasius, and William the Librarian, would have lost their senses entirely if they had thought they could bury, by the effort of their silence and their shame, a filth that is supposed to have so filled Rome with astonishment, indignation and scandal that she could find satisfaction only by perpetuating the effect of her just disdain, and by setting up lasting marks for posterity: the erection of a statue representing the cause of her spite, the diversion of her processions, and the introduction of customs unheard of before and not at all decent.

units.la: Mais tant s'en faut que l'on ayt daigné prendre les choses de ce biais, on a fait gloire de verifier que si la faveur a peu de venë, la haine & la colere n'en ont point du tout. L'auteur de l'erreur populaire publié sous le nom du Sr. de Remond, emporté par la tourmente de cette mauvaise passion, a fait ce qu'il a peu pour se rendre indigne de toute creance. 1. En supposant des choses entierement fausses. Comme quand il soustient que trois, voire quatre cens ans durant nul n'a parlé de la Papesse, combien que Marianus n'ayt pas esté eloigné de deux cens ans du temps auquel on pense qu'elle a vescu : quand il traduit Schedel ennemy formel des Hussites comme imbu de leurs sentimens : quand il accuse Clauser (pour la bonne foy duquel parle l'edition Grecque de Chalcondyle) d'avoir inseré du sien dans la version Latine le discours de la Papesse ; quand il asseure que Musée cite les Sibylles ; quand il veut faire passer pour Anglois Constanti[?] le Grand, decedé 124 ans devant la premiere irruption des Anglois dans la grande de Bretagne ; quand il nie qu'Otton de[?] Frisinghen, qui fait mention expresse de[?] la Papesse au 35 chap. du 7 livre, en ayant[?] rien escrit : quand il attribue à l'Empereur[?] Valens un Lieutenant nommé Bartes, quand il veut qu'Anastase le Bibliothecaire, soit ce prestre Cardinal qui fut condamné l'an 853 par le Pape Leon I V, & depuis oppose à Benoist I I I : quand il qualifie François Vincent de Lerins, mort auparavant que les François fussent parvenus dans la Gaule jusques à la Seine : quand il escrit que le livret de Benno imité par Sigebert, mort des le 5 Octob. 1113, a esté suppose du temps de Luther : quand (directement au contraire du certificat des Historiens Ecclesiastiques) il attribue au Concile de Nicée d'avoir fait & confir-mé les loix du Celibat : quand il impute aux Allemans (qu'il depeint comme excessivement addonnez à la paillardise) qu'eux seuls ont fait mention de la Papesse ;
